articleTitle: Contrastive Learning for Cold Start Recommendation with Adaptive Feature Fusion
publicationTitle: 2025 5th International Conference on Consumer Electronics and Computer Engineering (ICCECE)
abstract: This paper proposes a cold start recommendation model that integrates contrastive learning, aiming to solve the problem of performance degradation of recommendation systems in cold start scenarios due to the scarcity of user and item interaction data. The model dynamically adjusts the weights of key features through an adaptive feature selection module and effectively integrates user attributes, item meta-information and contextual features by combining a multimodal feature fusion mechanism, thereby improving recommendation performance. In addition, the model introduces a contrastive learning mechanism to enhance the robustness and generalization ability of feature representation by constructing positive and negative sample pairs. Experiments are conducted on the MovieLens-1M dataset. The results show that the proposed model significantly outperforms mainstream recommendation methods such as Matrix Factorization, LightGBM, DeepFM, and AutoRec in terms of HR, NDCG, MRR, and Recall, especially in cold start scenarios. Ablation experiments further verify the key role of each module in improving model performance, and the learning rate sensitivity analysis shows that a moderate learning rate is crucial to the optimization effect of the model. This study not only provides a new solution to the cold start problem but also provides an important reference for the application of contrastive learning in recommendation systems. In the future, this model is expected to play a role in a wider range of scenarios, such as real-time recommendation and cross-domain recommendation.

articleTitle: Optimized Unet with Attention Mechanism for Multi-Scale Semantic Segmentation
publicationTitle: 2025 5th International Conference on Consumer Electronics and Computer Engineering (ICCECE)
abstract: Semantic segmentation is one of the core tasks in the field of computer vision, and its goal is to accurately classify each pixel in an image. The traditional Unet model achieves efficient feature extraction and fusion through an encoder-decoder structure, but it still has certain limitations when dealing with complex backgrounds, long-distance dependencies, and multi-scale targets. To this end, this paper proposes an improved Unet model combined with an attention mechanism, introduces channel attention and spatial attention modules, enhances the model's ability to focus on important features, and optimizes skip connections through a multi-scale feature fusion strategy, thereby improving the combination of global semantic information and fine-grained features. The experiment is based on the Cityscapes dataset and compared with classic models such as FCN, SegNet, DeepLabv3+, and PSPNet. The improved model performs well in terms of mIoU and pixel accuracy (PA), reaching 76.5% and 95.3% respectively. The experimental results verify the superiority of this method in dealing with complex scenes and blurred target boundaries. In addition, this paper discusses the potential of the improved model in practical applications and future expansion directions, indicating that it has broad application value in fields such as autonomous driving, remote sensing image analysis, and medical image processing.

articleTitle: Tomato Maturity Detection in Complex Orchard Environment
publicationTitle: 2025 5th International Conference on Consumer Electronics and Computer Engineering (ICCECE)
abstract: This paper presents a model for detecting tomato maturity called EFC-YOLO11. It utilizes the C3k2-EMSDCEEM, C3k2-Faster, and C-BiFPN modules to enhance feature extraction, multi-scale feature fusion, and detection accuracy. The model also demonstrates strong adaptability to different conditions and good generalization ability. In experiments using the PF500 dataset, it shows a 2.5% improvement in mAP50 and a 3.7% improvement in mAP50-95. On the Chunxiang variety dataset, it improves mAP50 by 2.1 % and mAP50-95 by 2.4%. Additionally, in the purple passion fruit detection task, the model increases recall by 5.2%. The overall mAP50 reaches 86%.

articleTitle: Design Optimization of Low-Power Microelectronic Circuits Based on CMOS Technology
publicationTitle: 2025 5th International Conference on Consumer Electronics and Computer Engineering (ICCECE)
abstract: As a renewable energy technology, photovoltaic power transmission has important value in meeting energy demand and reducing environmental pollution. This paper optimizes and designs a low-power consumption and high-reliability transmission scheme based on CMOS integrated circuits. The combination of current-limiting NMOS transistors and additional bias voltage regulation enables precise control of circuit operating current, effectively reducing power consumption and improving energy conversion efficiency. In addition, this paper draws on the optimization method of low-power sample-and-hold circuits, and takes advantage of the characteristics of low leakage current and low quiescent power consumption of CMOS devices to optimize the voltage detection and energy storage module while ensuring system stability. Experimental results show that the optimized design can flexibly adjust the switching voltage and working current to ensure the efficient operation of the system under the condition of low power consumption, and is suitable for small equipment application scenarios such as implantable bioelectronic devices and IoT micronodes.

articleTitle: STSR: An Efficient Model for Super-Resolution Reconstruction
publicationTitle: 2025 5th International Conference on Consumer Electronics and Computer Engineering (ICCECE)
abstract: STSR is an efficient and lightweight super-resolution model built upon the Swin Transformer architecture. By utilizing the hierarchical window-based self-attention mechanism of the Swin Transformer, STSR effectively captures global contextual information while ensuring high computational efficiency. To further enhance its performance and reduce model complexity, we incorporate lightweight design elements and residual structures. These improvements not only facilitate better gradient flow but also significantly boost the recovery of high-frequency details. Experimental results on the DIV2K dataset show that STSR delivers exceptional performance, significantly reducing both parameter count and computational costs.

articleTitle: Research and Implementation of Obtaining Monitoring Indicators for Redis Cluster in Distributed Systems
publicationTitle: 2025 5th International Conference on Consumer Electronics and Computer Engineering (ICCECE)
abstract: This paper focuses on the research and implement of obtaining monitoring indicators for Redis cluster in distributed systems. With the rapid development of distributed systems, Redis cluster has become an essential component for handling large - scale data and high - concurrent access. By effectively monitoring Redis cluster, we can ensure its stable operation, optimize performance, and quickly detect and solve potential problems. This paper first analyzes the architecture and working principle of Redis cluster, then elaborates on the key monitoring indicators and their significance. Next, it presents a comprehensive acquisition scheme, including data collection, transmission, and storage methods based on the prometheus. Finally, through experimental verification, the effectiveness and feasibility of the proposed scheme are demonstrated.

articleTitle: An Integrated Positioning Method Based on Weighted Factor Graph Optimization
publicationTitle: 2025 5th International Conference on Consumer Electronics and Computer Engineering (ICCECE)
abstract: The intelligent transportation system requires positioning services to ensure safe driving applications. The fusion positioning method of GNSS and inertial navigation system (INS) provides high-precision location services in environments with good GNSS signal reception. However, in satellite signal denial environments such as tunnels, GNSS signals become weak or interrupted due to obstructions, resulting in a decline in observation quality or even making the signals unavailable, which leads to a sharp deterioration in positioning accuracy. Ground-based navigation system can serve as a supplement and enhancement to GNSS, offering a solution for continuous high-precision positioning both inside and outside tunnels, as well as in enclosed spaces. To address the above issues, this study proposes a weighted factor graph optimization algorithm that integrates inertial navigation and ground-based navigation. Based on the traditional factor graph model, weighted factors are introduced to reduce the impact of outlier observations on positioning results, enhance the model's anti-interference and fault tolerance capabilities, and improve the system's positioning performance. The sliding window optimization method is employed to reduce computational complexity while retaining effective historical data, improving computational speed, and ensuring real-time positioning output. Simulation results indicate that, compared with unweighted factor graph positioning schemes, the proposed integrated positioning algorithm improves positioning accuracy by 75.8%, while significantly reducing the computational load of information fusion.

articleTitle: Human Activity Recognition Using STFT and Attention-Enhanced 2D-CNN on Smartphone and Wearable Sensors
publicationTitle: 2025 5th International Conference on Consumer Electronics and Computer Engineering (ICCECE)
abstract: Traditional Human Activity Recognition (HAR) approaches often rely on handcrafted features and incomplete feature extraction, limiting their effectiveness. To address these challenges, we propose a 2D Convolutional Neural Network (2D-CNN) model with an attention mechanism, incorporating Short-Time Fourier Transform (STFT) to convert raw time-series sensor data into time-frequency representations, enabling richer spatiotemporal feature extraction. The 2D-CNN is designed to capture hierarchical patterns, while the Triplet Attention mechanism learns cross-dimensional dependencies. The proposed framework is evaluated on three widely used HAR datasets, WISDM, UCI-HAR, and PAMAP2, achieving classification accuracies of 96.65%, 96.3%, and 97.32%. Experimental results demonstrate that our method outperforms existing deep learning models, delivering improved recognition accuracy and robustness across diverse activities.

articleTitle: Joint Task Offloading and UAV Deployment for Collaborative HAP-UAV Systems
publicationTitle: 2025 5th International Conference on Consumer Electronics and Computer Engineering (ICCECE)
abstract: In emergency scenarios such as natural disasters, unmanned aerial vehicles (UAVs) are widely employed to provide communication and computation services when ground infrastructure fails. However, UAVs face limitations in resources. High Altitude Platforms (HAPs), operating in the stratosphere, offer a promising solution with their wide coverage and substantial payload capacity. This paper proposes a collaborative task offloading scheme that combines UAVs and HAPs to minimize task delays, considering task types and the mobility of ground devices, which are typically overlooked. We jointly optimize UAV deployment and task scheduling, modeling deployment as a maximum clique problem and task scheduling as a device-UAV matching problem solved by a stable matching algorithm. Numerical simulations demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed solution.

articleTitle: Energy and Reliability aware Cloud Workflow Scheduling with Uncertain Task Execution Times
publicationTitle: 2025 5th International Conference on Consumer Electronics and Computer Engineering (ICCECE)
abstract: Energy consumption and reliability are crucial for cloud workflow scheduling, and many methods have been proposed to address these issues. However, these methods typically assume that task execution times are deterministic, and the problem of reliably scheduling workflows with uncertain task execution times while minimizing energy consumption has not yet been studied. To address this gap, this paper proposes a new algorithm named EWSR, which consists of three phases: workflow analysis, task scheduling, and online adjustment. The algorithm ensures the reliability of cloud workflows under uncertain task execution times while simultaneously reducing energy consumption. An online adjustment mechanism is designed to dynamically adjust task reliability and release idle resources, thereby increasing resource utilization while lowering energy consumption. Experimental results demonstrate that EWSR effectively reduces energy consumption while meeting workflow reliability requirements.

articleTitle: EC-YOLO: Enhanced YOLOv10 for Agricultural Pest Detection
publicationTitle: 2025 5th International Conference on Consumer Electronics and Computer Engineering (ICCECE)
abstract: Agricultural pests pose a significant threat to agricultural production. There is an urgent need for efficient and accurate pest detection methods to guide rational pesticide application. Traditional pest detection relies on on-site inspections by experts, which are costly and inefficient. In recent years, deep learning technologies have made substantial progress in pest recognition but still struggle with detecting multiple types of pests in complex natural environments. To address these challenges, this paper introduces a new model based on YOLOv10, called ECYOLO, which makes the following key improvements:Firstly, this paper designed an Edge Information Perception Enhancement module to replace the traditional Cross Stage Partial Bottleneck with 2 Convolutions module. This module integrates multi-scale pooling branches and edge information extractor module, effectively capturing multi-scale features and edge information in images. Secondly, this paper designed the Cross-Stage Weighted Feature Pyramid Network module, which fuses feature maps of different scales and employs an adaptive weighting mechanism to enhance the effectiveness of feature fusion.Experimental results indicate that EC-YOLO outperforms the YOLOv10 model on the IP102 datasets, with an mAP50 improvement of 2.6%, reaching 65.8%, and a recall improvement of 2.1<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">%</sup>, reaching 63.3%. Additionally, EC-YOLO surpasses six other popular object detection models, demonstrating superior performance.

articleTitle: HERO: A High-Efficient RISC-V Exploration and Optimization Framework
publicationTitle: 2025 5th International Conference on Consumer Electronics and Computer Engineering (ICCECE)
abstract: RISC-V is a reduced instruction set architecture (ISA) known for its modular design, simplicity, and portability, making it suitable for a wide range of applications, from small embedded systems to large-scale computers. BOOM[7] is a microprocessor based on the RISC- V architecture, featuring numerous adjustable parameters, which complicates manual tuning. Efficient and accurate optimization of its parameter space has posed a significant challenge for designers. This study introduces HERO: A High-Efficient RISC-V Exploration and Optimization Framework, an automated design space exploration framework that addresses the parameter optimization issues encountered with processors like BOOM. Experimental results indicate that the TPE algorithm utilized in the HERO framework enhances tuning outcomes for the target value (the product of processor performance metrics, specifically cycles and power consumption) by 1.4% compared to Randomized Algorithm[IS], by 3.3% compared to Quasi-Monte Carlo (QMC) [16]and Genetic Algorithms (GA)[17], and by 20.8% compared to Human Effort[18], thereby achieving efficient and high-performance automated tuning.

articleTitle: Continual Learning Based on Multi-Teacher Knowledge Distillation
publicationTitle: 2025 5th International Conference on Consumer Electronics and Computer Engineering (ICCECE)
abstract: Continual learning aims to enable models to progressively acquire knowledge from novel classes while preserving existing knowledge without catastrophic forgetting of old classes. To achieve this objective, continual learning must operate under three critical constraints: limited training samples per new class, consistent computational costs for learning new classes, and linear memory growth proportional to the number of known classes. To address these constraints, this paper proposes DM-FSCIL (Distillation-MLP Few-Shot Class-Incremental Learning), an architecture comprising three auxiliary teacher networks, one trainable student network, and a dynamically expandable memory. The framework initially trains the student model on abundant base-class data. During incremental learning phases, it employs a multi-teacher knowledge distillation approach to train the network while storing encountered samples of all known classes. Subsequently, the system utilizes a multi-layer perceptron (MLP) module to aggregate base model predictions for student network calibration, effectively mitigating catastrophic forgetting. Comprehensive experiments conducted on Mini-ImageNet, CIFAR100, and CUB200 datasets demonstrate the framework's superior performance in few-shot continual learning scenarios.

articleTitle: Design and Implementation of a LoRa-Based Multi-Terminal Communication System
publicationTitle: 2025 5th International Conference on Consumer Electronics and Computer Engineering (ICCECE)
abstract: With the rapid development of the Internet of Things (IoT) technology, there is an increasing demand for communication. Long Range (LoRa) communication, as an emerging wide-area network communication technology, has been widely used in many fields by virtue of its unique advantages of low power consumption and long distance. This paper describes the design and realization of LoRa -based data transmission system, which adopts microcontroller as the control core, LoRa module as the transmission core, and adopts a variety of data interfaces to collect sensor data and realize low power consumption through power control circuit. Perform overall testing of the completed design system. The results show that the system successfully realizes the data transmission between multiple terminal nodes and gateways while also providing the system with low-power sleep function.

articleTitle: Butterfly Species Classification with EfficientNetB1 Transfer Learning
publicationTitle: 2025 5th International Conference on Consumer Electronics and Computer Engineering (ICCECE)
abstract: Butterflies, as vital pollinators and ecological indicators, play a significant role in maintaining biodiversity and ecosystem health. However, their survival is increasingly threatened by habitat loss and climate change, necessitating accurate species classification for effective conservation. This study aims to propose a classification method based on the principle of transfer learning, which employs the EfficientNetB1 model to achieve effective classification of multiple butterfly species. Leveraging a publicly available dataset comprising 6,499 images across 75 butterfly species, the model was fine-tuned to optimize performance. The dataset was divided into training, validation, and test sets with a ratio of 8: 1: 1, with stratified sampling ensuring balanced class distribution. The research findings reveal that the EfficientNetB1 model attains a classification accuracy of 91.4% on the test set. This study highlights the significant potential of deep learning techniques, particularly the EfficientNetB1 model, in advancing the identification and conservation of butterfly species. Furthermore, it emphasizes the critical role of such approaches in enhancing the understanding and application of deep learning for biodiversity monitoring and ecological preservation.

articleTitle: Performance Analysis of RIS Aided Wireless-Powered System for WBAN
publicationTitle: 2025 5th International Conference on Consumer Electronics and Computer Engineering (ICCECE)
abstract: Traditional wireless body area networks (WBAN) suffer from resource limitation problems, and the performance can be significantly affected by the channel. In this paper, we provide a reconfigurable intelligent surface (RIS) aided wireless-powered system for WBAN, which combines wireless energy transmission (WET) and wireless information transmission (WIT). This paper provides a precise theoretical analysis of the RIS-aided wireless-powered system over the Gamma distribution and log-normal distribution channels. In addition, moment matching is used to derive the outage probability and average age expressions of information. the effects of the distance between nodes and the signal-to-noise ratio (SNR) the transmitter on the system performance is analyzed. The theoretical analysis and simulation results show that RIS assists to improve the energy harvesting performance and enhance the signal strength and transmission efficiency.

articleTitle: Fontstyler: Artistic Font via Two-Stage Stylized Diffusion
publicationTitle: 2025 5th International Conference on Consumer Electronics and Computer Engineering (ICCECE)
abstract: Generating artistic fonts is significantly challenging because it requires a subtle balance between readability and artistic degree while presenting the visual expression of a specific subject in pretty and rational changes in the shapes and textures of target letters. While existing studies integrate the textures from subject reference images into target letters, the artistic degree and diversity of outcomes are constrained. By adopting Latent Diffusion Model (LDM), DS-Fusion generates more expressive and plentiful artistic fonts. Nonetheless, font structure fractures within DS-Fusion results. Furthermore, DS-Fusion may not sufficiently blend the semantics of the style prompt into the results. These issues undermine the aesthetic appeal and legibility of artistic fonts. To alleviate these issues, we introduce Fontstyler, an extension of DS-Fusion, employing a two-stage training process to blend style prompt semantics into target letters further and alleviate font structure fractures within DS-Fusion outputs. Specifically, we make LDM to blend prompt semantics into target letters by employing a CNN-based discriminator in the first training process. This discriminator discerns between the target letter image (considered real samples) and the outputs of reverse diffusion in LDM (considered fake samples). In the second training process, we take the results of the first training process as inputs to alleviate the font structure problem and improve the artistic degree of our model's results. We demonstrate the quality of our method on numerous examples and compare it to various baselines.

articleTitle: Nondestructive Detection of Cold Fresh Mutton Based on Hyperspectral Imaging Technology
publicationTitle: 2025 5th International Conference on Consumer Electronics and Computer Engineering (ICCECE)
abstract: The hygiene and safety quality of cold fresh lamb meat is of great significance for food safety control and ensuring the safety of residents' consumption. The quality parameters of lamb meat can be used to measure its hygiene and safety, but traditional testing methods have low efficiency and can also affect the sample during the testing process. The aim of this study is to achieve non-destructive testing of cold fresh lamb meat, using spectral technology to detect indicators related to volatile basic nitrogen (TVB-N), pH value, coliform count (MPN), and total bacterial count (TBC). The experimental results show that this technology can effectively distinguish cold fresh lamb meat of different quality states, and has high prediction accuracy for key quality indicators. The validation accuracy of the DNN model reaches 90.09%. Hyperspectral imaging technology provides a highly promising new approach for rapid, accurate, and non-destructive testing of cold fresh lamb, which is expected to be widely applied in meat processing, circulation, and sales, ensuring consumer safety and promoting high-quality development of the industry.

articleTitle: TN-YOLO: A YOLOv8-Based Algorithm for Extremely Small Defect Detection
publicationTitle: 2025 5th International Conference on Consumer Electronics and Computer Engineering (ICCECE)
abstract: Extremely small defect detection poses critical challenges in industrial quality inspection, particularly for defects characterized by micron-scale dimensions, irregular geometries, and low signal-to-noise ratios in complex backgrounds. While existing YOLO-series models suffer from feature degradation, redundant sampling, and noise amplification in such scenarios, this paper proposes TN-YOLO with three dedicated innovations: 1) The Adaptive Feature Integration (AFI) module employing learnable weights to maintain cross-level defect features; 2) The TNet neck optimizing feature fusion paths to preserve shallow spatial details; 3) The Normalized Channel Attention Mechanism (NCAM) leveraging dynamic channel-wise calibration to synergistically enhance defect features while suppressing background noise. Experimental validation on both a custom industrial wheel-hub DK dataset and the public SeaDronesSeev2 benchmark (specifically designed for extremely small objects) demonstrates TN-YOLO's superiority: 8.3% AP50 improvement over YOLOv8 on SeaDronesSeev2 while maintaining 36.6% mAP@[.50:.95] on DK-surpassing all compared models. The framework exhibits 19.7-20.4% relative improvement in mAP@[.50:.95], proving exceptional robustness in low-SNR environments. These advancements provide novel insights for small defect detection in industrial applications.

articleTitle: Research on the Security Assessment Method for Mimetic Multivariate Systems Based on Multi-Granularity Features
publicationTitle: 2025 5th International Conference on Consumer Electronics and Computer Engineering (ICCECE)
abstract: Aiming at the current status quo that the security assessment of mimetic multivariate systems generally adopts a single level of assessment, which is unable to establish a security link between its internal software diversity and the overall security of mimetic multivariate systems, this paper proposes an assessment mechanism that combines two assessment methods, namely, software diversity metrics under multi-granularity characterization and risk assessment of vulnerability attacking system modeling. The experimental part of the dataset uses the GNU core toolset (coreutils 8.32), and the validity of this assessment method is verified by designing a security assessment algorithm that weights and scores the heterogeneity of the multi-granularity software diversity technique, and then by modeling an attack on the mimetic multi-variant system experiment. The experimental results show that the security assessment algorithm can effectively assess the anti-attack ability and security of the mimetic multivariate system under the multi-granularity feature, which has certain reference value for the future research on the security assessment method of the mimetic multivariate system.

articleTitle: Research on Intelligent Algorithms for Path Planning of Driverless Vehicles and their Applications
publicationTitle: 2025 5th International Conference on Consumer Electronics and Computer Engineering (ICCECE)
abstract: Driverless technology is a crucial part of future intelligent transportation systems, and path planning is a core technology in driverless systems. This research aims to optimize existing path - planning algorithms and explore new ones. By collecting the latitude and longitude information of Chinese cities from public resources such as Baidu Maps, and after data cleaning, an inter - city distance dataset containing 1,048,574 records was constructed. The research compared the greedy algorithm, dynamic programming, and their derivative algorithms, and selected the Euclidean distance to calculate the distance between points. The results show that there are significant differences in the performance of different algorithms. The Greedy Kruskal algorithm performs relatively well among the greedy algorithm family, and the combination of dynamic programming and the Bellman - Ford algorithm stands out. Based on this, a two - stage intelligent optimization algorithm for driverless vehicles was designed. The first stage uses the Bellman - Ford algorithm for preliminary path planning, and the second stage optimizes the path with the Kruskal algorithm. This algorithm combines the advantages of different algorithms, providing a more effective solution for path planning of driverless vehicles, and is of great significance for promoting the development of autonomous driving technology and constructing intelligent transportation systems.

articleTitle: Graph Convolutional Networks with Visual Masking and Social Interaction Models for Pedestrian Trajectory Prediction
publicationTitle: 2025 5th International Conference on Consumer Electronics and Computer Engineering (ICCECE)
abstract: Pedestrian trajectory prediction is critical for autonomous driving, crowd analysis, and urban surveillance. To address insufficient interaction modeling in existing methods, we propose two enhancements. First, a field-of-view(FoV)-aware masking mechanism filters irrelevant interactions by dynamically adjusting to pedestrian distances and motion directions. Second, we introduce a more detailed modeling of the influence among pedestrians, replacing the traditional modeling based on reciprocal of distance. This model, integrated with FoV masks to construct sparse adjacency matrices for graph convolution. A temporal convolutional network then predicts trajectories as bivariate Gaussian distributions. Evaluations on ETH and UCY benchmarks demonstrate the effectiveness of our method.

articleTitle: A Monitoring Method Based on EEG Data and Deep Learning
publicationTitle: 2025 5th International Conference on Consumer Electronics and Computer Engineering (ICCECE)
abstract: In the context of modern education, the pursuit of effective teaching and learning has been constantly evolving. With the increasing emphasis on personalized education and the need to understand students' cognitive processes in real-time, the limitations of traditional teaching assessment methods have become more prominent. This paper presents a monitoring method for real-time assessment of students' classroom understanding based on EEG data and deep learning. By addressing the limitations of traditional teaching assessment methods, this approach aims to provide educators with more accurate and timely feedback. The proposed method utilizes specific EEG data, advanced data processing techniques, and deep learning algorithms to achieve high-accuracy monitoring.

articleTitle: A Big Data-Based Multidimensional Analysis and Optimization Framework for Physical Education
publicationTitle: 2025 5th International Conference on Consumer Electronics and Computer Engineering (ICCECE)
abstract: This study explores the application of big data technology in physical education, developing an efficient and intelligent data analysis framework. By leveraging multidimensional motion data collection and analysis, combined with key techniques such as 3D directional energy feature extraction and motion template matching, the research achieves precise identification and correction of sports movements. To enhance algorithm performance, the study introduces optimization strategies, including hierarchical energy feature extraction, adaptive template matching, and temporal consistency checks, effectively reducing computational complexity while improving real-time performance and accuracy. Experimental results demonstrate that the optimized model significantly outperforms the baseline, with a 3%-5% improvement in detection resolution, a 30% reduction in processing time, and a 40% decrease in error rates. This research not only provides theoretical support and technical assurance for the reform of physical education models but also lays a foundation for the development of intelligent physical education. Future advancements integrating artificial intelligence technologies can further drive personalized and intelligent teaching practices.

articleTitle: Research on End-to-End Image Dehazing Algorithm Based on Ultra-Lightweight Network Architectures for Efficient Visual Enhancement
publicationTitle: 2025 5th International Conference on Consumer Electronics and Computer Engineering (ICCECE)
abstract: It is a common problem in computer vision applications in which the visibility of images is reduced due to haze, and lots of detail is lost. To solve this problem, we propose an end-to-end single-image de hazing algorithm based on ultra-lightweight network architecture, which combines the existing advance methods and innovates based on this to achieve efficient visual enhancement. Inspired from the recent advances in existing deep learning-based dehazing models, we introduce a multi-scale feature extraction module which helps capture local and global cues related to haze with computational efficiency. The integration of residual learning strategy and attention mechanism refines the model in the process of dehazing and improves the accuracy of dehazing with the lightweight and high efficiency retained. Furthermore, the hybrid loss function is optimized to achieve a harmony between pixel-level accuracy and perceptual quality. The experimental results indicate that the proposed model outperforms the existing dehazing models in terms of visual quality and computational efficiency.

articleTitle: Multi Scale SAR Image Target Detection Algorithm Based on RT-DETR
publicationTitle: 2025 5th International Conference on Consumer Electronics and Computer Engineering (ICCECE)
abstract: To address low detection accuracy in SAR images due to complex backgrounds, large scale variations, and small targets, an improved algorithm SRA-DETR based on RT-DETR is proposed. It uses repBlock on four backbone branches to reduce parameters and enhance speed, incorporates a self-attention vision transformer for feature similarity extraction, and employs SE-CBAM for small target detection to suppress background interference. Adaptive path downsampling improves feature retention and background filtering compared to nearest neighbor methods. SRA-DETR decreases parameters by 40% and computational complexity by 20%, achieving aP50 of 96.6% and increasing mAP from 77.9% to 80.1% over the original RT-DETR.

articleTitle: A Simple Single Channel Type k Thermocouple Temperature Measurement Design
publicationTitle: 2025 5th International Conference on Consumer Electronics and Computer Engineering (ICCECE)
abstract: Thermocouples are widely used in the field of industrial production and are characterized by their simple structure, durability and wide range of applicable temperatures. For the multi-channel thermocouple temperature measurement circuit design is relatively complex, and most of the designs do not have a USB interface, which may be inconvenient to use. This paper proposes a simple single channel type k thermocouple thermometer with USB interface, which can read the temperature data directly through the host computer software. A thermostatic bath was used to test the design, and the experimental results showed that the accuracy of the design was better than 0.08%, which satisfied the design requirement of not less than 0.2% accuracy.

articleTitle: LabEYE: A System to Support Eyetracking Laboratory Experiment Research
publicationTitle: 2025 5th International Conference on Consumer Electronics and Computer Engineering (ICCECE)
abstract: This paper proposes a system that allows researchers to manage laboratory experiment research based on eye tracking with complete auxiliary functions of the experimental process, including recruitment and registration, experimental arrangement, preparation of experimental materials, design of areas of interest, experiments and analysis of data. In addition, the system mainly achieves the drawing and analysis of Areas of Interest (AOI). The main AOI module adopts the Faster RCNN object detection algorithm, the text region detection algorithm, the face detection algorithm, and builds the DBSCAN clustering algorithm, thereby enabling automatic drawing of AOIs for different types. It utilizes the OpenCV image processing library to realize manual drawing of AOIs. Experimental results demonstrate that this system is simple and user-friendly, enhancing the efficiency of AOI drawing. Additionally, it offers researchers effective research guidance and management methods, improving their work efficiency.

articleTitle: Exploration of Sustainable Crop Cultivation Strategies Under Resource Constraints Based on Integration of Simulation and Algorithms
publicationTitle: 2025 5th International Conference on Consumer Electronics and Computer Engineering (ICCECE)
abstract: With the increasing concern for sustainable agriculture and efficient resource utilization, the study of crop planting strategy optimization under resource constraints has become an important topic. In this paper, an integrated framework combining simulation and optimization algorithms is proposed for developing sustainable crop cultivation strategies. A 0–1 linear programming model is constructed to maximize economic returns under resource constraints, taking into account constraints such as land area, crop rotation, and resource allocation. A simulated annealing algorithm was introduced to optimize the minimum planting area allocation of a single plot to ensure the rationality of spatial and temporal distribution. Based on the 2023 data of a rural area in the mountainous region of North China, the optimal planting strategies from 2024 to 2030 were predicted. The results show that the proposed method significantly improves resource utilization efficiency, ensures the stability of economic returns, and flexibly adapts to different resource constraint scenarios. This study provides theoretical support for sustainable agricultural development and useful reference for land use optimization.

articleTitle: Personalized Clothing Pattern Generation Driven by Body Shape Data
publicationTitle: 2025 5th International Conference on Consumer Electronics and Computer Engineering (ICCECE)
abstract: Addressing the inefficiencies of existing pattern- making techniques and their inability to meet personalized demands, this paper investigates an automated method for generating personalized garment patterns based on human body size information. Utilizing methods such as LASSO regression, spline functions, and neural networks, we establish a model capable of automatically extracting key features from human data and pattern templates to produce size-adaptable garment patterns. Specifically, multi-factor LASSO regression is employed to extract significant features from body measurements, spline functions are used to fit garment pattern lines and extract garment feature points, and finally, neural networks are applied to integrate human and garment features to obtain adaptively scaled fashion patterns. Through ablation experiments, the model's high predictive accuracy is demonstrated. The implementation of this project will provide a new technological approach to achieving automation and personalization in the garment industry.

articleTitle: Design and Verification of Multi-Channel PP-MVT Digitizers for Enhanced Photodetection
publicationTitle: 2025 5th International Conference on Consumer Electronics and Computer Engineering (ICCECE)
abstract: Photodetection systems rely on precise pulse sampling to achieve accurate detection, which is crucial for highprecision applications such as positron emission tomography (PET) and LiDAR. To improve pulse sampling accuracy, the peak-picking multi-voltage threshold (PP-MVT) method incorporates peak information into the conventional MVT method, thereby enhancing pulse recovery accuracy and energy resolution (ER). However, for multi-channel PP-MVT digitizers, traditional analog to digital converters (ADCs) either increase the cost per channel or limit the counting rate, which restricts the scalability and deployment. To address this critical technical challenge, we design and verify a multi-channel PP-MVT digitizer which digitizes solely through time-to-digital converters (TDCs) with minimal extra hardware usage of only 6 IO per channel. To demonstrate the feasibility, we implemented a single-channel prototype, achieving peak picking accuracy with a RMSE<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">t</inf>of 4.79 ns and a RMSE<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">v</inf>of 22.20 mV. Additionally, using an LYSO/SiPM photon detector under the radiation of a <sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">22</sup>Na source, the PP-MVT digitizer demonstrated superior and more stable sampling performance compared to the conventional MVT method. This work establishes a foundation for scalable multi-channel PP-MVT digitizers, demonstrating potential for highdemand photo detection systems.

articleTitle: Based on the Application and Research of Artificial Intelligence in Medical Diagnosis and Treatment
publicationTitle: 2025 5th International Conference on Consumer Electronics and Computer Engineering (ICCECE)
abstract: With the rapid development of artificial intelligence technology, its application in medical diagnosis and treatment is increasingly extensive. In this paper, an intelligent diagnosis system based on convolutional neural network (CNN) and long short-term memory network (LSTM) is proposed to solve the problems of high misdiagnosis rate and low data processing efficiency in traditional medical diagnosis methods. By optimizing the convolutional layer structure of CNN and the hidden layer design of LSTM, the accuracy of the proposed system on the MNIST medical image dataset and MIME-III electronic medical record dataset reached 95.6% and 91.5%, respectively, which was significantly higher than the traditional method (85.4<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">%</sup> and 84.7%)[1]. The experimental results show that the system in this paper is superior to the existing studies in accuracy, recall rate and AUC value, especially when dealing with complex cases. In addition, this paper further improves the training efficiency and generalization ability of the model by introducing data enhancement and early stop method. This study provides a new technical means for the application of artificial intelligence in the medical field, which has important theoretical significance and practical application value.

articleTitle: MXene Quantum Dot/Perovskite-based Memristor with Tunable Switching Characteristics for Artificial Intelligence Technology
publicationTitle: 2025 5th International Conference on Consumer Electronics and Computer Engineering (ICCECE)
abstract: In this study, Ag/Nb2C QDs/MAPbI3/ITO memristor based on MAPbI3 perovskite materials combined with MXene quantum dots (Nb2C QDs) as a resistive switching layer was successfully prepared, which realized the systematic memristor function under certain electrical injection. The relevant results show that the memristor device has threshold switching (TS) characteristics at low compliant current (Icc) and resistance switching (RS) characteristics at high Icc. Besides, the device achieves a low SET voltage (~0.85 V), a high on/off ratio (~10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>), and an ultra-steep switching slope (~0.231 mY/dec). These results indicate that this memristor device has great application potential in artificial intelligence technology with low power consumption and high computing efficiency.

articleTitle: Research and Application of Intermediate Experiment Digitization Basic Platform
publicationTitle: 2025 5th International Conference on Consumer Electronics and Computer Engineering (ICCECE)
abstract: This paper focuses on the development and application of an intelligent basic platform for intermediate experiments, serving the oil production process. Through a series of methods such as hardware intelligent upgrading and transformation, establishing connections between programmable logic controllers and hardware devices based on Modbus protocol, designing configuration software to read and control display data in real time, the intelligent basic platform for intermediate experiments has been successfully developed. The research and development achievements include the design and completion of three sets of configuration systems, intelligent control of hardware working status, and real-time data reading and graphical display, providing efficient and intelligent platform support for experimental research in the industry.

articleTitle: Research on Automatic Regulation of Focused Ion Beam Parameters Based on Image Scoring
publicationTitle: 2025 5th International Conference on Consumer Electronics and Computer Engineering (ICCECE)
abstract: AI's advancement prioritizes industrial automation for resource efficiency and control accuracy. SEMs, evolving with semiconductor tech, now shift from manual to auto-control. Our paper introduces an auto-algorithm for SEM focus and fine-tuning, featuring image quality scoring and parameter adjustment. Using Python, we analyze image edges, gray values, contrast, and noise, refining parameters for clarity. Our method adaptively adjusts parameter steps based on image scores, accelerating convergence to optimal values, thus enhancing automation and efficiency in industrial applications.

articleTitle: A High Accuracy Readout Circuit for Resistor Array
publicationTitle: 2025 5th International Conference on Consumer Electronics and Computer Engineering (ICCECE)
abstract: This article presents a new method for measuring two dimensional piezoresistive arrays, reducing operational amplifier (opamp) usage while enhancing measurement accuracy. The offset voltage of opamp causes significant current crosstalk in the array readout circuit, reducing measurement accuracy. To reduce errors caused by opamps, a method using fewer opamps and modifying the power supply excitation is proposed. As a result, the precision of resistance measurements is enhanced without increasing circuit complexity. Theoretical analysis has demonstrated that this design can enhance both the stability and accuracy of the measurement. Simulation analysis verified that this approach can achieve higher measurement accuracy than the zero potential method (ZPM) on a 16 × 16 resistor array as the mean, variance, and coefficient of variation of the offset voltage of the opamps are adjusted, and can reduce errors by more than 50%. Both theoretical study and simulation analysis were validated through experimental measurements.

articleTitle: Research on Control of Winch Type Heave Compensation System Based on Speed Prediction of SVR
publicationTitle: 2025 5th International Conference on Consumer Electronics and Computer Engineering (ICCECE)
abstract: Taking the energy-saving winch-type heave compensation system suitable for actual working conditions as the application object, a practical method for predicting the heave motion speed of a floating platform is studied. With the goal of improving the compensation accuracy of the compensation system, the support vector regression(SVR) model is used to predict the speed and the prediction results are used for compensation control. Firstly, the ITTC dual-parameter spectrum is used to obtain the wave spectrum under different levels of sea conditions, and according to the transmission relationship between the floating platform and the waves, the displacement and velocity data of the heave motion of the waves and the floating platform under different levels of sea conditions are simulated; secondly, the Library for Support Vector Machines(LIBSVM) toolbox are used to predict the heave motion speed of the floating platform in the next prediction cycle; finally, a combined simulation model of the energy-saving winch-type heave compensation system suitable for actual working conditions is built. The simulation results show that the method of using platform speed prediction for disturbance compensation control can improve the compensation accuracy.

articleTitle: A Multi-Head Attention-Based Method for Internet of Things Device Identification
publicationTitle: 2025 5th International Conference on Consumer Electronics and Computer Engineering (ICCECE)
abstract: With the gradual increase in the number of devices in the Internet of Things (IoT), accurate identification of devices has become crucial. Existing methods primarily rely on communication protocols, behavior characteristics, and traffic fingerprints, often failing to fully exploit the temporal characteristics of data traffic. This study proposes an IoT device identification method based on Multi-Head Attention. By extracting protocol features and packet features from traffic data, the method utilizes a multi-head attention mechanism to capture temporal features of packets, thereby achieving effective device identification. Experimental results demonstrate that the proposed method achieves a comprehensive recognition accuracy of over 97% on the Aalto dataset.

articleTitle: Intelligent Recognition Assisted Medicine Box for Aging
publicationTitle: 2025 5th International Conference on Consumer Electronics and Computer Engineering (ICCECE)
abstract: Aiming at the problem of timely and safe medication for the elderly, this paper uses STM32 as the main control Microcontroller Unit and JETSON nano as the image processing module, and designs a set of automatic pet feeding system using WiFi communication for remote control. The user remotely reminds the elderly to take medication in time through the sound module, and after the medicine box recognizes the face of the elderly and unlocks it, it passes the data through the serial port to the STM32, which controls the stepping motor to open and close according to the received signals, realizing the intelligent and safe taking of medication. While STM32 controls the operation of the motor, STM32 and the relay will feed back to the user according to the current recorded residual weight, realizing the process of changing and taking medicine in time. The system runs stably and is able to strictly execute the process of supervising the medication taking; it is highly malleable, transplantable and convenient to use.

articleTitle: DLA-Deformable DETR: Dynamic Layer Assignment Deformable DETR for Remote Sensing Images
publicationTitle: 2025 5th International Conference on Consumer Electronics and Computer Engineering (ICCECE)
abstract: The rapid advancement of remote sensing technology has made extracting accurate information from remote sensing images increasingly challenging due to multi-scale object distribution, object sparsity, and complex backgrounds. To address these challenges, we propose the Bi-directional Cross Stage Partial Feature Pyramid Network (BCSPFPN), which enhances the integration of high-level semantic features and low-level fine-grained features. We also introduce the Dilated Convolution Pyramid Module (DCPM) to improve the model's ability to capture high-level semantic information and detect small objects. Additionally, the Dynamically Allocated Deformable Decoder (DA-Deformable Decoder) dynamically allocates features from different levels to the decoder, addressing early-stage feature extraction issues. Experiments on the NWPU VHR-10 and RSOD datasets demonstrate that our method achieves state-of-the-art performance in object detection.

articleTitle: Application of Data Hiding Method Based on Triplet Difference in QR Code Images
publicationTitle: 2025 5th International Conference on Consumer Electronics and Computer Engineering (ICCECE)
abstract: Ensuring the privacy and security of sensitive information is paramount in the digital age. Quick response (QR) codes, known for their high data density and robust error correction capabilities, have become widely used, making them an ideal medium for secure data transmission. This paper introduces a novel data hiding method based on triplet differences, designed to embed secret information within QR code images. The proposed method manipulates the differences between pixel triplets in the QR code matrix, achieving high payload capacity while maintaining the structural integrity and readability of the QR code. By leveraging the inherent redundancy of the QR code matrix, this technique imperceptibly encodes hidden data and resists various forms of image processing attacks. Performance is evaluated based on data capacity, imperceptibility, and robustness to errors. Experimental results demonstrate that the triplet difference method significantly outperforms traditional data hiding techniques in terms of efficiency and security. This study highlights the potential applications of the triplet difference method in secure information sharing, digital watermarking, and authentication, paving the way for advanced data hiding techniques that enhance the security and practicality of QR code technology.

articleTitle: Research on Electronic Signal Feature Extraction and Classification Based on Machine Learning
publicationTitle: 2025 5th International Conference on Consumer Electronics and Computer Engineering (ICCECE)
abstract: This paper presents a new approach to extracting and classifying electronic signals based on deep learning. Combining the merits of CNN and LSTM, a hybrid neural network structure is proposed to extract features. Finally, the validity and innovation of this algorithm are proved by experiment. The experimental dataset includes many kinds of electronic signals, including communication and industry control. Experiments show that this method can improve the precision of feature extraction by 25%. The precision of classification is 92.5%, the recall rate is 91.8%, and the F1 score is 92.2%. Compared with other methods, the proposed algorithm has better anti-interference capability and higher computing efficiency.

articleTitle: Remote Environmental Monitoring Based on Beidou Mobile Monitoring Terminal with an Early Warning Platform
publicationTitle: 2025 5th International Conference on Consumer Electronics and Computer Engineering (ICCECE)
abstract: With the increasingly serious environmental problems, traditional monitoring methods are faced with challenges such as poor real-time performance and insufficient data accuracy. Based on the Beidou Navigation Satellite System (BDS) and mobile monitoring terminal, a remote environmental monitoring and early warning platform is designed in this paper. The platform combines Beidou positioning, sensor data acquisition, wireless communication and cloud computing analysis to monitor and warn environmental changes in real time. By integrating the Beidou positioning module, the platform is able to accurately obtain the location of equipment and collect environmental data such as climate, air quality and noise, and ensure stable operation in remote areas using low-power wide-area networks such as NB-loT. Experimental results show that the platform performs well in terms of data acquisition, transmission efficiency and early warning accuracy.

articleTitle: A Compensation Model for Optical Encoders at Various Speeds Based on Improved DQN
publicationTitle: 2025 5th International Conference on Consumer Electronics and Computer Engineering (ICCECE)
abstract: To address the issue of error compensation for optical encoders in various measurement environments, a compensation model based on an improved deep reinforcement learning (DRL) framework has been designed. This marks the first attempt to introduce DRL into the compensation problem of optical encoders. To achieve this, an improved deep Q-learning network (DQN) has been developed to construct the compensation model. Specifically, the network enhances measurement accuracy by first compensating the input grating images and then cascading with a positioning and decoding network. Experimental results demonstrate that the designed compensation network is suitable for various speed measurement environments, and the measurement accuracy achieved using this compensation network surpasses that of existing compensation methods.

articleTitle: Exploration on Communication Technologies for Automatic Fire Alarm Systems in the Petrochemical Industry
publicationTitle: 2025 5th International Conference on Consumer Electronics and Computer Engineering (ICCECE)
abstract: Currently, the automatic fire alarm systems installed and used in the petrochemical industry adopt the same bus communication technology as those in civil buildings. However, due to the higher requirements for communication reliability and more severe electromagnetic interference in petrochemical sites, problems such as data transmission errors, communication interruptions, false alarms, and system crashes frequently occur during bus communication. This paper analyzes the communication problems existing in the automatic fire alarm systems applied in the petrochemical industry and proposes solutions from a standardization perspective.

articleTitle: Ensemble Empirical Mode Decomposition with Approximate Entropy: A Novel Detection Model for QUIC Anomaly Traffic
publicationTitle: 2025 5th International Conference on Consumer Electronics and Computer Engineering (ICCECE)
abstract: With the rise of Web3.0 and the continuous development of blockchain technology, traditional transmission protocols such as TCP and UDP are gradually unable to meet the growing demand for network applications. Quick UDP Internet Connection (QUIC) stands out with its multiple features such as low latency and support for multiplexing. However, new network attack methods continue to emerge, and how to accurately identify abnormal network traffic has become an extremely important challenge. Because QUIC traffic has the self-similarity, this research proposes an abnormal traffic detection model based on Ensemble Empirical Mode Decomposition (EEMD) and Approximate Entropy (ApEn). By adaptively decomposing traffic, mining abnormal traffic features, and adding ApEn method to reduce component complexit. Finally, it is determined whether the QUIC transmission network is under attack by comparing the changes in Hurst values before and after the attack. This paper uses the NS-3 platform to implement and evaluate this solution. Experiments have verified that the model proposed in this research can better solve the problems of traditional methods in terms of poor adaptability and low efficiency, and has a high accuracy rate in detecting abnormal traffic, making it suitable for network traffic attack detection.

articleTitle: Comparative Analysis of Sparse Multinomial Logistic Regression and Convolutional Neural Networks for Multi-Class Image Classification
publicationTitle: 2025 5th International Conference on Consumer Electronics and Computer Engineering (ICCECE)
abstract: The classification problem represents a funda-mental challenge in machine learning, with logistic regression serving as a traditional yet widely utilized method across various scientific disciplines. The current popular method for solving multi classification problems is deep neural networks, especially convolutional neural networks. However, as the number of neural network layers increases, the hardware requirements for model solving will be very high. Therefore, it is meaningful to study methods for multi classification problems with limited computing resources. In this study, we proposed using semidefinite proximal alternating direction method of multipliers(spADMM) to solve the multinomial logistic regression model and compared it with convolutional neural network models. Our results demonstrate that the spADMM not only achieves comparable accuracy to several prevalent convolutional neural network models but also ex- hibits significant improvements in time efficiency with limited computing resources.

Author Keywords: Semidefinite proximal alternating direction method of multi-pliers

articleTitle: A Dynamic Adaptive Data Filtering and Sampling Framework for Optimized Fine-Tuning of Large Language Models
publicationTitle: 2025 5th International Conference on Consumer Electronics and Computer Engineering (ICCECE)
abstract: Fine-tuning large language models (LLMs), such as Baichuan2-7B, faces challenges in data quality and training efficiency. This paper introduces DADFS (Dynamic Adaptive Data Filtering and Sampling), a new framework designed to optimize LLM fine-tuning. DADFS includes three components: Dynamic Adaptive Filtering (DAF), Adaptive Data Sampling (ADS), and Data Mixing and Proportional Weighting. The framework filters training data based on quality scores to ensure high-quality and diverse samples. It also uses adaptive sampling to select the most informative data points for training and employs data mixing to improve generalization and reduce overfitting. Experimental results show that DADFS outperforms traditional fine-tuning methods across key metrics. DADFS also integrates LoRA (Low-Rank Adaptation) within the PEFT (Parameter-Efficient Fine-Tuning) framework, which helps maintain computational efficiency while improving model adaptability and stability. This research offers an efficient and scalable solution for LLM fine-tuning, showing the importance of data optimization for model performance.

articleTitle: An Improved Adaptive Whale Optimization Algorithm with Multi-Strategy for Optimization Problems
publicationTitle: 2025 5th International Conference on Consumer Electronics and Computer Engineering (ICCECE)
abstract: The Whale Optimization Algorithm (WOA) is indeed recognized for its effectiveness in solving complex optimization problems, including NP-hard problems. However, like many metaheuristic algorithms, it has its limitations. Insufficient population diversity and ineffective search strategies are common challenges that can reduce its performance. We urgently need to introduce effective strategies to alleviate these core shortcomings of WOA. To address the slow convergence, low accuracy, and local optima issues of WOA, this paper proposes an Improved Adaptive Whale Optimization Algorithm with multi-strategy(IWOA). Firstly, enhanced Sine chaotic map was introduced to improve the quality of the initial population. Secondly, the adaptive inertia weights are used to balance the global and local searches, so as to accelerate the convergence of the algorithm. Lastly, the Metropolis criterion is incorporated to strengthen the algorithm's ability to escape local optima. Datasets are used to verify the performance of the improved adaptive whale optimization algorithm in solving problems.

articleTitle: Generalizable Negation Detection: Addressing the Challenges of Cross-Domain Data with Data Augmentation
publicationTitle: 2025 5th International Conference on Consumer Electronics and Computer Engineering (ICCECE)
abstract: Negation poses significant challenges for modern natural language processing (NLP) models, such as bidirectional encoder representations from transformers (BERT), often leading to misinterpretations. While the robust optimized BERT pre-training method (RoBERTa) is an optimized version of the BERT model, its ability to detect and interpret negations is limited, especially in complex linguistic and cross-domain environments. This work proposes a fine-tuning approach that utilizes counterfactual data augmentation (CDA) to improve the performance of the RoBERTa model in understanding and detecting negation. The proposed method incorporates both original and counterfactual samples, along with supplementary corpus generated by large language models (LLMs). By combining these diverse datasets, the approach improves the RoBERTa model's sensitivity to negation and its generalization across domains. Experimental results show that the developed approach taps the potential of counterfactual augmentation techniques to advance the NLP systems in addressing the challenges of negation.

articleTitle: Efficient Grey Wolf: High-Performance Optimization for Reduced Memory Usage and Accelerated Convergence
publicationTitle: 2025 5th International Conference on Consumer Electronics and Computer Engineering (ICCECE)
abstract: This paper presents an efficient Grey Wolf Optimizer (EGWO) designed to address the limitations of the standard Grey Wolf Optimizer (GWO), focusing on reducing memory usage and accelerating convergence. The proposed method integrates Sinusoidal Mapping for enhanced population diversity and a Transverse Longitudinal Crossover strategy to balance global exploration and local exploitation. These innovations improve search efficiency and optimization precision while maintaining a lightweight computational footprint. Experimental evaluations on 16 benchmark functions demonstrate EGWO's superior performance in convergence speed, solution accuracy, and robustness. Its application to hyperparameter tuning of a Random Forest model for a housing price dataset confirms its practical utility, further supported by SHAP-based interpretability analysis.

articleTitle: DAF-Net: A Dual Attention Fusion Network with Window-Guided Attention and Invertible Modules for Infrared-Visible Image Fusion
publicationTitle: 2025 5th International Conference on Consumer Electronics and Computer Engineering (ICCECE)
abstract: Infrared and visible image fusion plays a pivotal role in mission-critical vision systems by combining complementary thermal radiation and textural information. While deep learning approaches have advanced beyond traditional multi-scale decomposition methods, existing solutions face fundamental limitations: convolutional neural networks (CNNs) inadequately model long-range dependencies, while vision transformers suffer from computational complexity and local feature extraction deficiencies. To address these challengesWe propose a Dual Attention Fusion Network (DAF-Net) featuring three key components: (1) A hybrid encoder combining convolutional and window-based attention operations to process both global thermal patterns and local textures, (2) An invertible fusion module that preserves critical features during modality integration, and (3) A multi-scale architecture maintaining spatial consistency through efficient depth-wise convolutions and attention-guided connections. Experimental results show that our method achieves competitive performance in standard metrics, outperforming both classical fusion baselines and recent advanced approaches, while maintaining computational efficiency comparable to mainstream CNN-based methods.

articleTitle: Code Reuse Attack Detection Based on Hardware and Software Performance Counters
publicationTitle: 2025 5th International Conference on Consumer Electronics and Computer Engineering (ICCECE)
abstract: Currently, with the continuous development of code reuse attack, it has become a mainstream attack, how to defend or detect this attack has become a research hotspot in the security field. Most of the existing techniques have the problems of high overhead and limited detection scope, for this reason, this paper proposes a code reuse attack detection method based on hardware and software performance counters, which realizes efficient and low overhead code reuse attack detection by collecting the number of selected event occurrences from the system wide. This method significantly improves the efficiency and accuracy of attack detection by training a GRU-SVM neural network model, utilizing GRU to extract time-series features, and combining the accurate classification capability of SVM. Meanwhile, this paper utilizes the sensitive system call records to determine the possible location of the attack through the sensitive system call records after the attack is detected. The experiments conducted reveal that the proposed strategy ensures precise identification capabilities, maintains low computational resource consumption, and is adaptable to diverse scenarios. This presents a reliable and efficient pathway for mitigating risks associated with code reuse vulnerabilities.

articleTitle: Design and Implementation of a Low-Power TCAM Controller Based on Bloom Filter
publicationTitle: 2025 5th International Conference on Consumer Electronics and Computer Engineering (ICCECE)
abstract: Ternary Content Addressable Memory (TCAM) has a wide range of applications in network packet filtering, route lookup, and other scenarios due to its extremely fast lookup speed. However, the high storage cost and power consumption of TCAM limit its application in large-scale deployment. To address this challenge, this paper proposes a Bloom Filter-based low-power TCAM controller (BF-LPTCAM) design scheme, which aims to reduce the storage cost and power consumption of TCAM while maintaining its efficient data matching capability. In this paper, a pipelined structure is used to filter the looked-up TCAM cells using logical table partitioning method and Bloom filtering technique to support the storage and look-up of 80/160/320 bits of data. In this paper, RTL implementation, functional simulation and logic synthesis are carried out for the algorithm, which can save at least more than 83.2 % power consumption and storage utilisation can be better without matching entries in TCAM. Under the TSMC 7nm process, the system can support a 1GHz frequency clock and a single lookup operation takes only 40ns.

articleTitle: ELL-ORB-SLAM: Improved Robust Monocular Visual SLAM Algorithm Based on Image Enhancement and Dynamic FAST Threshold for Low-light Environment
publicationTitle: 2025 5th International Conference on Consumer Electronics and Computer Engineering (ICCECE)
abstract: The accuracy of visual localization estimation heavily relies on the quality of input images and feature point extraction, with variations in illumination significantly impacting matching results under challenging conditions. To address this, we propose an enhanced ORB-SLAM algorithm (ELL-ORB-SLAM) based on dynamic adaptive FAST thresholds and image enhancement techniques, including illumination map estimation, improved Truncated Adaptive Gamma Correction, and CLAHE, to improve performance in low-light conditions and refine feature point extraction. Experiments conducted on the EuRoC, KITTI, and ETH3D datasets demonstrate that ELL-ORB-SLAM significantly outperforms the state-of-the-art ORB-SLAM3, particularly in challenging environments. Additionally, real-world tests using a monocular camera showcase the system's robustness and versatility across diverse settings.

articleTitle: Improving Visual Reinforcement Learning via Spatial-Temporal Data Augmentation
publicationTitle: 2025 5th International Conference on Consumer Electronics and Computer Engineering (ICCECE)
abstract: Sample efficiency has been a challenging problem in visual reinforcement learning, where agents not only learn polices but also extract meaningful state representations for decision making from images. Reinforcement Learning methods that adopt data augmentation have significantly improved sample efficiency. However, prior studies have primarily focused on spatial augmentation, which enhances data diversity but insufficiently exploits temporal information, such as historical states which is critical for time-series-dependent reinforcement learning tasks. To address this gap, we introduce a Spatial-Temporal Data Augmentation (STDA) framework designed to enhance the agent's ability to learn task-relevant state representations by effectively leveraging historical state information. We evaluate our approach using the DeepMind Control Suite, and empirical results demonstrate that STDA significantly improves performance, surpassing state-of-the-art methods across a range of tasks.

articleTitle: The Research on Abstractive Summarization Method Based on Topic Model and Contrastive Learning
publicationTitle: 2025 5th International Conference on Consumer Electronics and Computer Engineering (ICCECE)
abstract: In the field of text summarization, generative models based on Transformer have made significant progress. However, they suffer from exposure bias and loss of global semantic information when processing text. This paper proposes a text summarization method based on topic models and contrastive learning. By introducing topic models to obtain the relationship between words and latent topics, and designing an alignment function to fuse the representation vectors generated by the topic model with the input text representation, it ensures that topic information is effectively utilized by the model. In addition, contrastive learning is used to adjust the model's loss function, bridging the gap between the training and inference stages, effectively alleviating the exposure bias problem. Experimental results on the NLPCC dataset show that this method effectively alleviates the exposure bias problem and retains key information in the text, achieving higher ROUGE scores.

articleTitle: Urban Waterlogging Disaster Assessment Based on Vision Transformer
publicationTitle: 2025 5th International Conference on Consumer Electronics and Computer Engineering (ICCECE)
abstract: With the accelerated pace of urbanization, the frequency and intensity of extreme rainfall events in cities are increasing, leading to frequent flooding disasters. Accurately estimating water accumulation information during floods is crucial for effective disaster prevention and mitigation. This study proposes an urban waterlogging disaster prediction model based on Vision Transformer (ViT), categorizing waterlogging severity into four levels: level_O (no waterlogging), level_l (mild waterlogging), level_ 2 (moderate waterlogging), and level_ 3 (severe waterlogging). The model was trained and tested using 2,230 images collected from the internet, along with data augmentation operations. Experimental results demonstrate that the model achieves an average recognition accuracy of 92.79% across all categories, with outstanding performance in level_ 0 and level_3 classifications. This high-accuracy model provides an effective technical means for rapid assessment and response to urban waterlogging disasters, significantly enhancing urban flood disaster management efficiency and emergency response capabilities.

articleTitle: High-Speed 3D Motion Attitude Measurement Technology Based on a Monocular Vision Multi-camera Array
publicationTitle: 2025 5th International Conference on Consumer Electronics and Computer Engineering (ICCECE)
abstract: In response to the limitations in usage scenarios and low camera utilization of 3D pose measurement methods based on binocular vision or multiple camera intersections for high-speed moving objects, a 3D motion pose measurement method using a monocular vision high-speed camera array is adopted. This paper proposes a monocular visual pose measurement algorithm for the object under test based on the <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$PnP$</tex> (Perspective-n-Point) algorithm. By constructing a likelihood function, the camera distortion coefficients are solved and optimized. Utilizing the one-to-one correspondence between the theoretical and actual coordinates of the object under test, the complete 3D motion pose of the object is obtained through an orthogonal iterative solution algorithm and a stitching algorithm. The mathematical models involved in this method and their derivation processes are introduced, and experiments are conducted to verify the effectiveness of the method.

articleTitle: LMAT-ND: A Meta-Attention-Enhanced Llama-7B Model for AI-Generated News Detection
publicationTitle: 2025 5th International Conference on Consumer Electronics and Computer Engineering (ICCECE)
abstract: This study introduces LMAT-ND (Llama-7B Enhanced Meta-Attention Transformer for News Detection) to distinguish AI-generated from human-authored news by integrating a Meta-Attention Mechanism and Dynamic Multi-Head Attention to capture linguistic distinctions, alongside a Dual-Classification Layer for optimized classification. LMAT-ND leverages Meta-Attention to dynamically adjust attention distribution, enhancing context-aware feature extraction, while the Dynamic Multi-Head Attention refines classification by emphasizing context-sensitive features. Additionally, the Dual-Classification Layer employs a two-stage strategy, integrating semantic and linguistic details to improve predictions. Experiments demonstrate that LMAT-ND outperforms GPT-3 and Llama-7B in accuracy, recall, and F1-score, with ablation studies confirming the Meta-Attention Mechanism and Dual-Classification Layer's impact. Performance remains strong across COCO and FakeImage datasets, validating its effectiveness in AI-generated content detection. Future work will focus on refining borderline case handling and extending applicability to broader AI-generated content detection tasks, further enhancing adaptability and robustness.

articleTitle: SECoT: Security-Oriented Chain-of-Thought Make Large Language Models Safer
publicationTitle: 2025 5th International Conference on Consumer Electronics and Computer Engineering (ICCECE)
abstract: The problem of harmful content generation in LLMs arises from the varied and intricate nature of their training data. Although filtering mechanisms are employed during pre-training, completely eliminating the impact of harmful content remains challenging. Additionally, the open-ended generation nature of the model during the inference phase further complicates content control. Therefore, how to effectively constrain the model's output while preserving its generative capabilities has become a critical topic in current AI safety research. Emerging research has revealed that the Chain of Thought (CoT) prompting strategy plays a pivotal role in augmenting the problem-solving abilities of large language models (LLMs). By guiding these models to generate intermediate reasoning steps, CoT facilitates a more structured approach to addressing intricate tasks, particularly in fields like mathematics and programming. This advanced reasoning ability provides new pathways for enhancing the safety of LLMs. This research introduces a Security-Oriented Chain of Thought (SECoT) mechanism. The SECoT framework consists of three parts: analyzing the safety of the problem, reflecting on the safety strategies involved, and formulating strategies to answer the problem, ultimately providing a final safe answer based on the above analysis, safety strategies, and response strategies. The SECoT process ensures that the response is not only well-considered but also safe. Building on this, a high-quality SECoT dataset (each entry includes five components: question, safety analysis, safety strategy, response principle, and safe answer) is further constructed and used as fine-tuning data to fine-tune LLMs in an end-to-end manner. Experimental results show that the SECoT framework enhances the safety of content generated by LLMs during the inference phase.
