Experimental results show that the proposed method achieves 95.5%, 71.9%, 93.2%, 86.4%, and 400 for mAP50, mAP50-95, Precision, Recall, and FPS, respectively, on the UDOD dataset. These results outperform detection algorithms such as YOLOv7, Fast R-CNN, and YOLOv8s. Furthermore, compared to the baseline model YOLOv8n, the proposed method improves the AP50 by 4.9% and the frame rate (FPS) by 43. In conclusion, the DE-YOLOv8n model facilitates real-time, high-precision dead fish detection and provides effective technical support for underwater robots in deep-sea net-pen aquaculture.

articleTitle: Multi-Scale Feature Aggregation Attention for Pancreatic Segmentation
publicationTitle: 2025 5th International Conference on Consumer Electronics and Computer Engineering (ICCECE)
abstract: Accurate pancreatic segmentation of CT images is very important for the observation and intervention of pancreatic cancer. However, due to the complex location and small volume of the pancreas, this task presents significant challenges. To address these issues, we propose a novel multi-scale feature aggregation attention (MFAA) network, which integrates features from different kernels to enhance the performance of pancreatic segmentation. We evaluated our network on the NIH Pancreas dataset, and experimental results show that MFAA outperforms existing methods in multiple evaluation metrics and performs well across four metrics.

articleTitle: Analysis and Identification of Power Consumption Behavior of Industrial Users Based on Data Mining
publicationTitle: 2025 5th International Conference on Consumer Electronics and Computer Engineering (ICCECE)
abstract: In this paper, the Shanghai industrial users in some areas is studied to analyze its behavior of electricity through using data mining techniques. Based on the acquisition and integration of user profile data and electricity data, the data undergo repair and normalization processes. To enhance the K-means algorithm, the study considers two key factors: the number of clusters and the selection of initial cluster centers. The improved K-means algorithm is then applied to data classification to extract clustering characteristic curves for all user types. Subsequently, the typical electricity behavior characteristics are analyzed and compared with those obtained from the traditional K-means algorithm. Relevant indicators are introduced to evaluate the clustering performance. The results demonstrate that the improved K-means clustering algorithm effectively classifies different types of users and provides a more accurate and efficient analysis of user electricity behavior.

articleTitle: Improved Fuzzy Logic Inference Algorithm for Vital Sign Monitoring Using FMCW Radar*
publicationTitle: 2025 5th International Conference on Consumer Electronics and Computer Engineering (ICCECE)
abstract: Vital sign monitoring technology based on FMCW radar has become a research hotspot due to its high sensitivity and non-invasive nature. Compared to traditional methods, the fuzzy logic inference methods based on harmonic and intermodulation components proposed in recent years offer higher accuracy. However, these methods are more susceptible to interference from spurious peaks, making them highly sensitive to the configuration of membership functions, which limits the overall performance of the algorithm. To solve this problem, this paper proposes an improved fuzzy logic algorithm based on multi-range bin combination (MRBCIFL). By jointly optimizing the signals from multiple range bins, the proposed algorithm effectively suppresses spurious peak interference and improves the quality of input data for fuzzy logic inference. Experimental results demonstrate that the MGCIFL method significantly improves the accuracy and robustness of heartbeat frequency estimation.

articleTitle: Efficient Communication Method for Hierarchical Federated Learning Based on 1-Bit Compressed Sensing
publicationTitle: 2025 5th International Conference on Consumer Electronics and Computer Engineering (ICCECE)
abstract: Federated learning is a distributed learning framework that allows multiple computing nodes to collaboratively train deep learning models without accessing each other's data. Under this framework, computing nodes transmit and aggregate model uploading with a common cloud server, efficiently completing deep learning training tasks. However, a major challenge currently faced by federated learning is the significant communication overhead generated by frequent model aggregation between computing nodes and the central server. Hierarchical federated learning is a novel federated learning framework that incorporates edge learning, introducing edge servers to enable model aggregation at the edge, thus avoiding the substantial communication cost incurred during aggregation between computing nodes and the central server. Several approaches have been proposed to reduce communication overhead in federated learning, including random sparsification and model quantization. In this work, they presented a 1-bit compressed sensing-based hierarchical federated learning algorithm for compressing communication models in hierarchical federated learning. The proposed algorithm significantly reduces the size of transmitted models during federated communication by performing sparsification, dimensionality reduction, and quantization on model updates. Experimental results on the MNIST and FashionMNIST dataset demonstrate that the proposed algorithm can significantly reduce communication overhead in hierarchical federated learning while ensuring virtually no performance degradation.

articleTitle: Research on the Location Planning of End-of-Life Vehicle Recycling Centers Based on Dual Objectives of Cost and Carbon Emissions
publicationTitle: 2025 5th International Conference on Consumer Electronics and Computer Engineering (ICCECE)
abstract: Background: With the increasing awareness of environmental protection and the rapid development of the automotive industry, the recycling and treatment of end-of-life vehicles (ELVs) have become pressing environmental issues. The recycling of ELVs not only involves resource reuse but also contributes to the reduction of carbon emissions. Objective: This study aims to explore the site selection problem of ELV recycling and processing centers based on dual objectives of cost and carbon emissions, and to propose an optimized site selection model that achieves a win-win situation for environmental protection and economic benefits. Method: In this study, the NSGA-II algorithm is used to model the site selection problem of ELV recycling and processing centers. The model takes into account factors such as transportation costs, processing costs, and carbon emissions. The objective function is designed to minimize both total costs and carbon emissions, while constraints are incorporated to ensure the feasibility of practical operations. Results: The results indicate that the proposed research plan can effectively reduce the total operating costs of enterprises while minimizing carbon emissions, achieving a dual optimization of both economic and environmental objectives for the entire transportation system.

articleTitle: EPN: Efficient and Balanced Network for Lightweight 2D Human Pose Estimation
publicationTitle: 2025 5th International Conference on Consumer Electronics and Computer Engineering (ICCECE)
abstract: With advances in deep learning, human pose estimation has seen significant progress. However, deep learning-based methods often increase parameter counts to boost accuracy, which leads to higher computational costs and restricts practical applications. In response, lightweight models for human pose estimation have been developed to lower computational demands, but they often suffer from reduced accuracy. To address this trade-off, we introduce the Efficient Pose Network (EPN), a novel 2D lightweight human pose estimation method. Our method incorporates innovative strategies in model architecture, training strategies, and keypoint detection. Extensive experiments demonstrate that EPN offers an outstanding balance of performance and efficiency, achieving high accuracy on the MPII dataset and SOTA results on the COCO dataset with identical parameter settings.

articleTitle: Transformer State Prediction Based on Deep Learning Network
publicationTitle: 2025 5th International Conference on Consumer Electronics and Computer Engineering (ICCECE)
abstract: As a crucial component of the power system, transformers state directly impacts the stable operation of the system. Accurately predicting the oil temperature of transformers can effectively prevent faults and improve equipment reliability. To make the system more stable, this article uses long short-term memory networks (LSTM) to predict transformer oil temperature. A predictive model was constructed by collecting and analyzing historical operational data, including factors such as current, voltage, load, and ambient temperature. We do plenty of experiments and prove our model performs better in predict accuracy and response speed in oil temperature prediction, and can better capture the temporal characteristics of oil temperature changes. It provides new ideas for transformer condition monitoring and intelligent maintenance, laying the foundation for the intelligent development of the power industry.

articleTitle: All-Inorganic Artificial Optical Synapse Based on CsPbBr3 QDs
publicationTitle: 2025 5th International Conference on Consumer Electronics and Computer Engineering (ICCECE)
abstract: In this work, CsPbBr3 QDs were successfully prepared and used as the functional layer of all-light-controlled synaptic devices with a two-terminal structure of Ag/CsPbBr3 QDs/FTO, which achieved systematic artificial synaptic functions under 405 nm and 532 nm light irradiation with the optical power of 4 mW. The typical synaptic properties including excitatory postsynaptic current (EPSC), pairing pulse facilitation (PPF), spike number-dependent plasticity (SNDP), and spike rate-dependent plasticity (SRDP) can be obtained. The short-term memory (STM) and long-term memory (LTM) phenomena can be observed through the SNDP measurement. Subsequently, the effects of different light wavelengths and powers on synaptic performance have been investigated. The consistency and durability of the all-light-controlled CsPbBr3 QDs-based synaptic device were tested, demonstrating good stability. Furthermore, we also explored the potential of CsPbBr3 QDs-based synaptic devices in convolutional neural networks (CNN) and studied the changes in image recognition accuracy under stimulation by light pulses of different wavelengths. After 50 trainings, the image recognition accuracy were 92.74% (405 nm) and 86.05% (532 nm), respectively. This study is expected to promote the development of artificial intelligence in the future.

articleTitle: A Structured Reasoning Framework for Unbalanced Data Classification Using Probabilistic Models
publicationTitle: 2025 5th International Conference on Consumer Electronics and Computer Engineering (ICCECE)
abstract: This paper studies a Markov network model for unbalanced data, aiming to solve the problems of classification bias and insufficient minority class recognition ability of traditional machine learning models in environments with uneven class distribution. By constructing joint probability distribution and conditional dependency, the model can achieve global modeling and reasoning optimization of sample categories. The study introduced marginal probability estimation and weighted loss optimization strategies, combined with regularization constraints and structured reasoning methods, effectively improving the generalization ability and robustness of the model. In the experimental stage, a real credit card fraud detection dataset was selected and compared with models such as logistic regression, support vector machine, random forest and XGBoost. The experimental results show that the Markov network performs well in indicators such as weighted accuracy, F1 score, and AUC-ROC, significantly outperforming traditional classification models, demonstrating its strong decision-making ability and applicability in unbalanced data scenarios. Future research can focus on efficient model training, structural optimization, and deep learning integration in large-scale unbalanced data environments and promote its wide application in practical applications such as financial risk control, medical diagnosis, and intelligent monitoring.

articleTitle: Multi - Level Attention and Contrastive Learning for Enhanced Text Classification with an Optimized Transformer
publicationTitle: 2025 5th International Conference on Consumer Electronics and Computer Engineering (ICCECE)
abstract: This paper studies a text classification algorithm based on an improved Transformer to improve the performance and efficiency of the model in text classification tasks. Aiming at the shortcomings of the traditional Transformer model in capturing deep semantic relationships and optimizing computational complexity., this paper introduces a multi-level attention mechanism and a contrastive learning strategy. The multi-level attention mechanism effectively models the global semantics and local features in the text by combining global attention with local attention; the contrastive learning strategy enhances the model's ability to distinguish between different categories by constructing positive and negative sample pairs while improving the classification effect. In addition., in order to improve the training and inference efficiency of the model on large-scale text data., this paper designs a lightweight module to optimize the feature transformation process and reduce the computational cost. Experimental results on the dataset show that the improved Transformer model outperforms the comparative models such as BiLSTM., CNN., standard Transformer., and BERT in terms of classification accuracy., Fl score., and recall rate., showing stronger semantic representation ability and generalization performance. The method proposed in this paper provides a new idea for algorithm optimization in the field of text classification and has good application potential and practical value. Future work will focus on studying the performance of this model in multi-category imbalanced datasets and cross-domain tasks and explore the integration with other technologies to further improve its performance.

articleTitle: Path Optimization in Quantum Networks Using Surface Codes
publicationTitle: 2025 5th International Conference on Consumer Electronics and Computer Engineering (ICCECE)
abstract: Surface codes have emerged as a promising approach for protecting quantum information against decoherence in quantum computation and communication. In this paper, we investigate the fundamental problem of path computation in quantum networks where surface codes are systematically employed in quantum information transmission. Specifically, we formulate the problem of finding a min-cost path subject to end-to-end fidelity constraint. The problem is non-trivial as only a subset of nodes in the network can perform coding and decoding operations due to its high cost, adding a combinatorial flavor to it. Our problem being NP-hard, we design an approximation path optimization algorithm by technically employing a discretization scheme allowing to bound the time and space complexity of the algorithm to be polynomial. We also demonstrate the effectiveness of our algorithm via extensive numerical analysis.

articleTitle: Study on the Selection of Empty Return Depot Location for Car Transport
publicationTitle: 2025 5th International Conference on Consumer Electronics and Computer Engineering (ICCECE)
abstract: This thesis focuses on vehicle logistics scheduling, aiming to improve transportation efficiency and reduce costs through demand forecasting and scheduling optimization. This paper reviews the domestic and foreign demand forecasting methods, points out the advantages of combined forecasting in improving accuracy, and puts forward a scheduling optimization model based on combined forecasting in view of the shortcomings of existing research on double-deck car scheduling and terminal location. By using Astar algorithm and integer linear programming (ILP), considering demand and distance comprehensively, the docking and no-load scheduling decisions are optimized, which solves the problem of traditional scheduling relying on experience. The effectiveness of the model is verified by an example analysis, which significantly reduces the transportation cost and improves the resource utilization rate. The research provides theoretical support and practical guidance for vehicle logistics scheduling, and the application of intelligent algorithm and environmental protection scheduling mode can be explored in the future.

articleTitle: Electrification Transformation and Cost Optimization of Logistics Vehicles through Efficient Slow and Fast Parameter Tuning
publicationTitle: 2025 5th International Conference on Consumer Electronics and Computer Engineering (ICCECE)
abstract: This paper addresses the issue of logistics vehicle electrification and cost optimization under urban traffic restriction conditions. A hybrid fleet scheduling and path optimization model based on the CPO algorithm and the SAFE framework is proposed. Experimental results show that the CPO-SAFE algorithm outperforms traditional CPO and ALNS algorithms in terms of optimization effectiveness and convergence speed, significantly enhancing the coordination efficiency between electric and fuel vehicles. Through case analysis, the effectiveness of government policies, such as road time window restrictions and carbon tax, is further validated.

articleTitle: Deep Learning-Based Multi-Modal Sentiment Analysis and Research
publicationTitle: 2025 5th International Conference on Consumer Electronics and Computer Engineering (ICCECE)
abstract: With the rise of social media and online platforms, the need for comprehensive analysis of multimodal data such as text, images, and audio has been increasing, making the effective fusion of these data crucial for the accuracy of sentiment analysis. However, existing multimodal sentiment analysis models often face issues with insufficient precision and low processing efficiency when dealing with complex data. To address these challenges, this paper introduces a new multimodal sentiment analysis model, the BLR model, which integrates Transformer and Bi-LSTM technologies to optimize the feature fusion process. Tests on standard datasets combined with the MVSA sub-datasetshow that the BLR framework enhances classification precision by 3.025% and 2.875% respectively, relative to conventional baselines. Moreover, ablation experiments confirm the BLR model's advantages in maintaining data integrity and enhancing processing efficiency, particularly in complex multimodal data handling tasks. These results not only demonstrate the advanced nature of the BLR model but also provide a new direction for future research in multimodal sentiment analysis.

articleTitle: Design Research on Smart Cane of YOLOv5s-Based Image Recognition and Vibration Feedback
publicationTitle: 2025 5th International Conference on Consumer Electronics and Computer Engineering (ICCECE)
abstract: Aiming at the severe challenges of the visual impairment in traveling, an intelligent cane integrating the optimized YOLOv5s image processing algorithm, wireless communication technology and multi-sensor detection technology is designed and implemented. The cane integrates the optimized YOLOv5 image processing algorithm and multiple sensor detection technologies, realizes the obstacle recognition of the cane, and has the functions of GPS positioning, voice prompts of road conditions and feedback. After actual scene testing, the cane performed well, fully met the design requirements, and significantly improved the mobility independence and social participation of the blind. It is of great significance to improve vision and quality of life.

articleTitle: Dual-LightGCN+: Enhanced Dual Light Graph Convolutional Network for Discriminative Recommendation
publicationTitle: 2025 5th International Conference on Consumer Electronics and Computer Engineering (ICCECE)
abstract: The Dual-LightGCN has shown promise in recommendation systems but faces limitations in explicitly modeling similarity signals between users and items, which restricts its ability to uncover potential relationships and negatively impacts recommendation performance. To address this, we propose an enhanced approach, Dual-LightGCN+ (DLGN+), which introduces edges between two-hop neighbors in the original user-item interaction graph to construct user-user and item-item graphs. This modification allows for more effective capture of similarity signals. Furthermore, we employ a sampling strategy that retains the maximum spanning tree of these newly constructed graphs, balancing the trade-off between information preservation and computational cost. This strategy substantially reduces both space and time complexity by selectively maintaining the most relevant similarity information. We evaluated DLGN+ on two datasets of varying sizes and compared it with several state-of-the-art recommendation algorithms. Experimental results demonstrate that DLGN+ outperforms the widely used methods in recommendation accuracy.

articleTitle: Optimizing Container Ship Stowage Planning with Yard Clash Considerations: Enhancing Yard and Quay Crane Coordination
publicationTitle: 2025 5th International Conference on Consumer Electronics and Computer Engineering (ICCECE)
abstract: Container ship stowage planning is a critical task that impacts the operational efficiency of both shipping companies and container terminals. This study addresses the often-overlooked issue of yard clashes, which are caused by the performance disparity between yard and quay cranes, hindering container retrieval and loading efficiency. We present the yard clash-aware stowage planning problem that integrates stowage planning and crane scheduling to minimize idle times of quay cranes. A mixed integer programming model, a just-in-time heuristic, and a genetic algorithm are developed to solve this complex problem. Numerical experiments demonstrate that while the mixed integer programming model struggles with large-scale instances, the just-in-time heuristic and genetic algorithm deliver competitive solutions with significantly reduced computation times. These findings highlight the potential of heuristic and metaheuristic approaches in addressing real-world operational challenges in maritime logistics.

articleTitle: Research Progress and Prospects of Obstacle Avoidance Technologies for Agricultural Unmanned Aerial Vehicles
publicationTitle: 2025 5th International Conference on Consumer Electronics and Computer Engineering (ICCECE)
abstract: With the rapid development of precision agriculture and smart agriculture, agricultural drones have demonstrated significant potential for application in the agricultural sector due to their efficiency and flexibility. However, agricultural drones face multiple challenges in practical operations, including complex environment perception, intricate data processing, and high-precision positioning, which limit the conversion of their potential into actual productivity. Therefore, the research and development of obstacle avoidance technology for agricultural drones is crucial. This study analyzes the current research progress in obstacle avoidance technology for agricultural drones, focusing on the application, advantages, and disadvantages of sensor technology in obstacle detection, innovations in environmental modeling technology to improve the accuracy of environmental understanding. The study also anticipates the development trends of obstacle avoidance technology for agricultural drones, suggesting that future research will concentrate on various combined obstacle avoidance forms to enhance the accuracy and robustness of obstacle avoidance, real-time active obstacle avoidance technology to adapt to more complex farmland environments, the development of obstacle avoidance assistance systems to improve user operating experience and work efficiency, and the standardization of obstacle avoidance processes to promote the standardization and industrialization of the technology.

articleTitle: Research on NFV-based Fault Diagnosis
publicationTitle: 2025 5th International Conference on Consumer Electronics and Computer Engineering (ICCECE)
abstract: Given the emergence of big data and Network technologies, it is difficult for traditional Network equipment and service capabilities to meet people's needs. The Network function Virtualization (Network function virtualization) decoupled the hardware and software from the virtualization of other services, thus reducing the cost of hardware and operation and maintenance and increasing the flexibility of services. In the environment of NFV, the network becomes extremely complex, and the hierarchical decoupling of network elements brings great challenges to fault detection and location. To solve this problem, this paper studies the fault diagnosis of NFV. Based on the research status of fault diagnosis, the network architecture, fault detection and location in the NFV environment were analyzed in detail, and the fault detection and location were studied by combining neural network, adaptive diagnosis, multi-layer network structure, Bayesian probability and other fault diagnosis methods. Finally, the future research direction of fault diagnosis is put forward, and the author thinks that multi-fault detection, rapid fault location and detection, and effective fault prediction algorithm will be the future research direction.

articleTitle: AIDetectVul: Software Vulnerability Detection Method Based on Feature Fusion of Pre-trained Models
publicationTitle: 2025 5th International Conference on Consumer Electronics and Computer Engineering (ICCECE)
abstract: Data-driven deep learning models are constrained by the scale and diversity of training data, making them vulnerable to data bias. While large language models (LLMs) exhibit superior generalization in vulnerability detection, their low inference efficiency and high computational costs hinder practical deployment in industrial settings. To address these limitations, we propose AIDetectVul, a novel vulnerability detection framework leveraging feature fusion from pre-trained models. Our approach concurrently utilizes encoder-only and decoder-only architectures to extract complementary code embeddings, with feature fusion enhancing semantic diversity. These enriched representations are then processed by a Transformer model, where the self-attention mechanism effectively captures long-range code dependencies, ultimately improving both detection accuracy and generalization capability. Comprehensive evaluations on proprietary enterprise datasets and open-source benchmarks demonstrate that AIDetectVul achieves comparable detection accuracy to the state-of-the-art LineVul model while demonstrating measurable improvements in generalization performance. Compared to LLM-based approaches, our solution maintains significantly lower computational overhead and training costs, making it particularly suitable for industrial applications.

articleTitle: Research on Constructing Image Stitching Models of Gigapixel Computational Imaging Systems
publicationTitle: 2025 5th International Conference on Consumer Electronics and Computer Engineering (ICCECE)
abstract: This paper addresses the issue of low accuracy in image stitching models and poor fused video quality in gigapixel computational imaging systems caused by feature-deficient areas in target scenes. An improved method is proposed, which obtains sample images from an array camera, performs region matching to determine initial positions, and calculates loss values to identify reference region pairs and classify regions as normal or abnormal. Abnormal regions are corrected through fitting, and image registration constructs the final stitching model. This approach improves model accuracy and scene-matching, enhancing fused video quality. Additionally, a fused video generation method is introduced, along with related devices, systems, and tools.

articleTitle: Improved Pedestrian Detection Algorithm for Traffic Vehicles Based on YOLOv8
publicationTitle: 2025 5th International Conference on Consumer Electronics and Computer Engineering (ICCECE)
abstract: This paper proposes an enhanced YOLOv8 framework for traffic object detection, specifically optimized for small and occluded targets in complex urban environments. The core improvements include: (1) SPD-Conv modules replace strided convolutions to preserve spatial features of blurred or small objects; (2) BiFormer dynamic sparse attention for background suppression; (3) an auxiliary 160x160 detection head for small targets; (4) N-IoU loss optimizing localization for overlapping objects. Evaluations on BDD100K demonstrate significant accuracy improvements: mAP@0.5 increases from 54.76% to 63.64% (+8.88pp) and mAP@0.5:0.95 from 32.62% to 40.16% (+7.54pp), while maintaining low complexity (3.8M parameters). Validation on KITTI confirms improved generalization, achieving 94.44% mAP@0.5. The balanced accuracy-efficiency trade-off makes this framework practical for autonomous driving deployments.

articleTitle: Research on Military Knowledge Graph Fusion Method Based on Multi-Technology
publicationTitle: 2025 5th International Conference on Consumer Electronics and Computer Engineering (ICCECE)
abstract: In the context of information warfare, the fusion of knowledge graphs in the military field is of great significance for assisting decision-making, intelligence analysis, and battlefield situational awareness. This paper proposes a method for constructing and applying military knowledge graphs based on multi-technology fusion, addressing the fusion issues between the CMNEE dataset and external knowledge graphs (such as CN-DBpedia). The method encompasses four key steps: data preprocessing, entity linking, graph construction, and graph fusion. By integrating technologies such as Stanford CoreNLP, TF-IDF with cosine similarity, Graph Convolutional Networks (GCN), BiLSTM + CRF models, and knowledge embedding (TransE), the fusion effect is significantly enhanced. Experimental results show that this method outperforms other combination methods across multiple metrics, providing strong support for military knowledge mining and application, with important practical significance and broad application prospects.

articleTitle: PriorSleepNet: Enhancing Sleep Stage Classification Through Prior Knowledge Integration
publicationTitle: 2025 5th International Conference on Consumer Electronics and Computer Engineering (ICCECE)
abstract: The basis for measuring sleep quality is the time distribution across different sleep stages. High-quality sleep should include sufficient sleep duration and a reasonable distribution of sleep stages. Therefore, sleep staging is a key indicator in sleep medicine. This paper introduces a novel sleep staging model, PriorSleepNet, which synergistically combines feature extraction, sequence modeling, and prior knowledge integration to achieve robust and physiologically consistent sleep staging classification. We use ResNet-34 to extract features from each 30-second sleep epoch, and then introduce a transformer structure as a sequence network to model the sequential information between epochs throughout the night. Unlike previous work that split the entire night's data into short sequences for processing, we pre-analyzed the distribution of sleep states as prior knowledge to address the issue of segmentation potentially losing the guiding role of preceding epochs. This allows us to use earlier sleep epochs to assist in determining the sleep stage at the beginning of the segments. Additionally, by modeling the complete sequence, we consider the dynamic changes and distribution of sleep states over time. PriorSleepNet collects labels for the entire night's sleep data, obtaining the statistical distribution of sleep stage counts at various times. This quantifiable prior knowledge of sleep patterns is introduced into the model to correct the model's erroneous staging results, thereby better reflecting biological sleep patterns. Experiment results show that the PriorSleepNet model has achieved excellent performance on the sleep dataset. Compared to existing methods, its staging accuracy has significantly improved, demonstrating the model's effectiveness and superiority in sleep staging tasks.

articleTitle: Label-Specific Feature Based Multi-Label Neural Network for Federated Learning
publicationTitle: 2025 5th International Conference on Consumer Electronics and Computer Engineering (ICCECE)
abstract: Federated learning (FL) enables the collaborative training of deep learning models across decentralized data sources (i.e., clients) while preserving data privacy by not requiring direct access to clients' training data. However, in the case of multi-label learning, the label correlations across clients are often diverse, which can disrupt the classification process. Direct application of an end-to-end classification model on each client may lead to inaccurate multi-label predictions due to these varying label dependencies across different clients. To resolve this issue, this paper begins by projecting the data and label information into a global feature space. Next, for each class, it retrieves the specific features related to that label from the global feature space, proactively mitigating inconsistent label correlations by focusing on label-specific features. Specifically, this paper proposes a label-specific approach: Label-Specific Feature-Based Multi-Label Federated Transformer (LSFT), where a distinct classification model is developed for each class on the clients. These models are constructed based on the Transformer and design label-specific classifier for each class based on the extracted features from the Transformer, which extract unique, label-specific discriminative features to alleviate the dependency on label correlation. Once gathered, these parameters are aggregated at the global model for each class, ensuring that the label correlations are properly aligned and minimizing interference, facilitating more effective multi-label federated learning framework. Through extensive experiments on various multi-label datasets (e.g., PASCAL VOC, MS-COCO), we demonstrate that the proposed model achieves competitive performance and outperforms standard federated learning methods in multi-label federated learning settings.

articleTitle: Research on the Design of an Artificial Intelligence-Based Cybersecurity Automatic Early Warning System
publicationTitle: 2025 5th International Conference on Consumer Electronics and Computer Engineering (ICCECE)
abstract: With the advent of the information age, cybersecurity issues have become increasingly severe. Traditional cybersecurity defense measures are no longer effective in addressing complex and dynamic security threats, making an artificial intelligence (AI)-based cybersecurity automatic early warning system a promising new research direction. This paper proposes the design and implementation of a cybersecurity automatic early warning system based on AI algorithms. The system collects network traffic data, analyzes potential security threats, and uses machine learning and deep learning algorithms to intelligently recognize and classify data, thereby detecting cyber attacks in real-time and issuing early warnings. This paper first reviews the current cybersecurity early warning technologies and, based on this, analyzes the applications of AI algorithms in cybersecurity. Subsequently, the functional requirements for a cybersecurity early warning system are discussed, followed by the design of system architecture and core algorithms. The proposed system's effectiveness and feasibility are validated through experiments and tests. Experimental results demonstrate that this system can accurately identify and issue warnings for various types of cyber attacks within a short timeframe, offering a high level of real-time performance and accuracy, thus providing effective technical support for cybersecurity.

articleTitle: Dynamic Optimization System for Dendrobium Officinale Cultivation Based on IoT Edge Computing and Hybrid Digital Twin
publicationTitle: 2025 5th International Conference on Consumer Electronics and Computer Engineering (ICCECE)
abstract: This study proposes an innovative Environment Control System (EDT-DHO) that optimizes the cultivation of Dendrobium officinale through the integration of Internet of Things edge computing and hybrid digital twin technology. The system breaks through three major bottlenecks: (1) Dynamic edge scheduling reduces delay from 287 seconds to 1823 seconds (a decrease of 36.5%); (2) Feature decoupling federated learning achieves a prediction accuracy of 92.7% with a privacy risk as low as 32%; (3) The FvCB-3DCNN hybrid model improves control precision to <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\pm 0.7^{\mathrm{o}}\mathrm{C}$</tex>. Cross-climate experiments show that the EDT-DHO system increases production by 23.6% and saves energy by 42.6%. Experiments demonstrate that the EDT-DHO provides a reproducible technical framework for the intelligent upgrade of precision agriculture.

articleTitle: Coherence Analysis of the Micro-Doppler Spectrum in Radar Echoes from Low-Altitude Rotor Targets
publicationTitle: 2025 5th International Conference on Consumer Electronics and Computer Engineering (ICCECE)
abstract: The small-amplitude motion of the target or its components, excluding the primary body translation, is referred to as micro-motion. This phenomenon reflects the subtle physical characteristics of the target, and its characterization holds significant importance in the feature extraction and the parameter estimation. This paper focuses on the micro-Doppler spectral characterization of a typical rotor target and systematically analyzes the radar echo modulation effects of the rotor. This is achieved by establishing a refined mathematical model of helicopter rotor echoes and deriving the frequency domain expression for the echoes produced by the rotating components. Through this derivation, a theoretical relationship between the target parameters and the micro-Doppler amplitude-phase characteristics is presented. The influence of the target parameters on the micro-Doppler characteristics is also analyzed, and the coherence of the micro-Doppler spectral lines of the target rotor echo is demonstrated. Finally, the validity of the theoretical analysis is confirmed through simulation experiments. This theory offers a novel approach for energy accumulation and feature extraction based on the coherence of the micro-Doppler spectrum.

articleTitle: An Improved YOLOv8-Based Method for Detecting Appearance Defects in Hull Closure Welds
publicationTitle: 2025 5th International Conference on Consumer Electronics and Computer Engineering (ICCECE)
abstract: This paper addresses the challenges of low efficiency and poor reliability in manual inspection of weld defects during ship manufacturing, proposing an improved YOLOv8-based detection method for hull closure weld appearance defects. By constructing a weld dataset containing five typical defects including cracks and pores, we innovatively integrate a Spatial and Channel Reconstruction Convolution (ScConv) module into the YOLOv8 backbone network. The spatial reconstruction unit and channel reconstruction unit effectively reduce feature redundancy while enhancing feature representation capability for micro-defects. Experimental results demonstrate that the improved model achieves 87% mAP50 on our proprietary dataset, with accuracy and recall rates reaching 87.8% and 86.4% respectively. Field deployment tests confirm a detection speed of 10.4s/m, showing 98.6% improvement in efficiency compared to traditional manual inspection (20.7s/m), thereby meeting real-time requirements. This method provides an automated solution for ship weld quality inspection with significant engineering application value.

articleTitle: Ordered Substrate Routing for High-Density Packaging Combining Improved Astar Algorithm
publicationTitle: 2025 5th International Conference on Consumer Electronics and Computer Engineering (ICCECE)
abstract: The substrate routing in high-density packaging boards is the physical connection foundation for various components. Optimizing substrate routing methods and technologies significantly enhances the performance and reliability of chips. Previous works have proposed numerous substrate routing algorithms. However, due to the discrepancies between actual routing results and expectations, manual adjustments are frequently necessary, coupled with prolonged routing times, which extend the design cycle. Therefore, in this paper, we propose a high-density packaging substrate routing algorithm based on ordered detailed routing. By pre-routing grouping of interconnections and order planning, as well as optimizing the Astar search algorithm, this paper aims to enhance overall routing capability and accelerate routing speed. The experimental results show that compared to Wen's routing algorithm, the proposed routing algorithm reduces the average wirelength by 1.1 % and routing time by 13.7% while maintaining the routability.

articleTitle: Capsule Networks with a Self-Attention Mechanism for Classification of Parkinson's Disase from Tremor
publicationTitle: 2025 5th International Conference on Consumer Electronics and Computer Engineering (ICCECE)
abstract: The traditional diagnosis of Parkinson's disease (PD)primarily relies on the Unified Parkinson's Disease Rating Scale and the clinical experience of physicians, leading to significant subjectivity in diagnosis. To address this issue, we employ sensor systems to collect tremor parameters from PD patients and analyzed these collected data using traditional machine learning algorithms, providing an objective and quantitative diagnosis for PD. To obtain more comprehensive features, this study adopts the PKG wearable device to extract 12 tremor features from 100 PD patients, along with recording 9 scale-based features and 3 demographic characteristics. Furthermore, to overcome the issues of low accuracy and poor generalization ability of traditional machine learning methods, we propose a capsule network integrated with a self-attention mechanism (SA-CapsNet) for classifying and predicting early stage and moderate to advanced stage stage PD patients. We also utilize the Synthetic Minority Over-sampling Technique (SMOTE) to improve the model's ability to generalize. Lastly, The Shapley Additive exPlanations (SHAP) model is introduced to improve the interpretability of the predictive model, and feature analysis is conducted to identify the main factors influencing classification and prediction. Experimental results demonstrate that the SA-CapsNet method for PD can achieve an accuracy of 92.31%, precision of 82.19%, recall of 91.23%, specificity of 80.00%, and an F1 score of 85.25%. Therefore, the proposed SACapsNet method not only exhibits good generalization ability for small sample sizes and imbalanced class data but also effectively assists physicians in staging the severity of PD.

articleTitle: A Blockchain-Based Medical Data Security Sharing Scheme Supporting Single-Factor Combined Authentication and Identity Privacy Protection
publicationTitle: 2025 5th International Conference on Consumer Electronics and Computer Engineering (ICCECE)
abstract: In the context of the rapid development of digital healthcare, achieving secure and verifiable medical data sharing has become a significant challenge. We propose a blockchain-based medical data sharing scheme that incorporates single-factor combined authentication and identity traceability, leveraging the transparency and immutability of blockchain. In this scheme, we propose a novel proxy re-encryption scheme that ensures user identity privacy, supports secure identity verification, and enables identity traceability under necessary conditions, as well as the secure distribution of keys. Additionally, our scheme uses groups to isolate business and resources, enhancing its flexibility and scalability. Through security analysis and experimental evaluation, we demonstrate that our scheme effectively resists chosen plaintext attacks while maintaining high efficiency and practicality.

articleTitle: A Survey of Granularity-Based Hardware Trojan Detection Methods for Gate-Level Netlists
publicationTitle: 2025 5th International Conference on Consumer Electronics and Computer Engineering (ICCECE)
abstract: Hardware Troj an (HT) detection is crucial for securing integrated circuits. This paper surveys extensive HT detection methods for gate-level netlists, categorized by granularity: single gate, sub-netlist, and full netlist. Single gate detection identifies anomalies in individual gates, sub-netlist detection examines local segments to detect HTs across interconnected gates, and full netlist detection assesses the entire netlist for HT presence. This paper summarizes these granularity-based methods, focusing on detection granularity, dataset, and results. For the frst time, we explore HT detection at the granularity level, providing an indepth perspective on gate-level netlist detection.

articleTitle: Temporal Feature Impact Explanation via Dynamic Sliding Window Sampling
publicationTitle: 2025 5th International Conference on Consumer Electronics and Computer Engineering (ICCECE)
abstract: Model interpretation methods are essential for understanding the predictions of machine learning models. How-ever, when applied to dynamic multivariate time series data, existing approaches encounter significant challenges, primarily due to the temporal correlations within the same feature at different time points. Ignoring temporal dependencies of time series data during interpretation usually leads to inadequate explanation results. To address these challenges, we propose a novel algorithm called Dynamic Sliding Window Sampling (DSWS) for explaining time series models. This algorithm dynam-ically generates importance scores for the same feature across various time steps by iteratively removing feature sets from specific time periods. Leveraging a sliding time window with an adaptable length, DSWS effectively captures the temporal dependencies of dynamic features and delineates their influence boundaries. Experiments on both synthetic and real world data sets validate DSWS’ applicability for time series data with dynamic temporal dependencies. Furthermore, it outperforms state-of-the-art methods in computational efficiency.

articleTitle: MBMRNet: Point Cloud Semantic Segmentation Based on Multi-branch Attention and Multi-resolution Feature Fusion
publicationTitle: 2025 5th International Conference on Consumer Electronics and Computer Engineering (ICCECE)
abstract: In the existing point cloud semantic segmentation methods, the study of local feature learning plays a dominant role. However, due to the absence of context information, the accuracy of semantic segmentation is seriously affected. In this study, we propose a novel network MBMRNet based on attention mechanisms. Firstly, we introduce the gradient information of point cloud and use relative position encoding to obtain spatial information. Then, we adjust the attention weight of different features by learning the point neighborhood and the relationship between different channels through a multi-branch attention (MBA) module. Finally, considering the differences between different resolution features at different stages, we design a multi-resolution feature fusion (MRFF) module to make full use of low resolution and high resolution features for dynamic point-level feature fusion. The experimental results on several public benchmarks demonstrate that MBMRNet outperforms existing methods, achieving 73.2% and 83.2% on the S3DIS Area 5 and NPM3D datasets, respectively.

articleTitle: C-CANet:Calibration-Based Cross-Modal Attention Network for Audio-Visual Event Localization
publicationTitle: 2025 5th International Conference on Consumer Electronics and Computer Engineering (ICCECE)
abstract: The task of Audio-Visual Event Localization (AVEL) aims to detect and locate the temporal segments of events through the interaction of audio and visual modalities. However, existing methods often suffer from redundant information interference during modality interactions, which limits the effectiveness of feature alignment and multimodal representation learning. To address this issue, we propose a novel Calibration-based Cross-modal Attention Network for Audio-Visual Event Localization. Specifically, we introduce a set of globally learnable tokens into the multihead attention mechanism of audio and visual modalities. These tokens act as intermediate bridges, actively aggregating and filtering critical information from multimodal features while effectively suppressing redundancy and irrelevant information. Through this approach, the model can achieve more efficient information exchange and alignment between audio and visual modalities, thus enhancing multimodal representation learning. Experimental results demonstrate that the proposed method significantly outperforms existing approaches on the challenge AVE dataset, especially in complex scenarios, exhibiting stronger robustness and generalization. Our research indicates that the introduction of learnable interaction tokens is an effective strategy for improving the efficiency and quality of information exchange in multimodal tasks, providing a new solution for audio-visual event localization.

articleTitle: Image Guided Lidar Point Cloud Completion Algorithm
publicationTitle: 2025 5th International Conference on Consumer Electronics and Computer Engineering (ICCECE)
abstract: To address the issues of severe information loss and suboptimal fusion effects in multimodal feature extraction and integration during point cloud shape completion using autoen-coder structures, which results in difficulty in balancing local and global feature information of point clouds and significant loss of structural information in images, this paper proposes a LiDAR point cloud multi-scale completion algorithm guided by image rotation attention mechanisms, with a focus on the study of feature extraction from point clouds and images. The network employs an encoder-decoder structure, where the image feature extractor in the encoder utilizes rotation attention mechanisms to enhance the capability of image feature extraction. The point cloud feature extractor employs multi-scale methods to improve the global and local information of point cloud features and employs multi-level self-attention mechanisms to achieve multimodal feature fusion. The decoder then employs a multi-branch completion method to accomplish the point cloud completion task, with the network trained using chamfer distance guidance. Comparatively, our algorithm outperforms eight related algorithms on the ShapeNet-ViPC dataset across various metrics. Compared to the state-of-the-art network XMFnet, the category-averaged Chamfer Distance (CD) value is reduced by 11.71%. The proposed algorithm in this paper can better extract image structural information, and the feature extraction of incomplete point clouds can consider both global and local information. Furthermore, through multi-level progressive feature fusion, the algorithm enhances the complementarity of information between different modalities, leading to more accurate point cloud completion results.

articleTitle: Transformer-based Multi-Object Tacking Long-term and Short-term Memory
publicationTitle: 2025 5th International Conference on Consumer Electronics and Computer Engineering (ICCECE)
abstract: Multi-Object Tracking (MOT) aims to capture the temporal dynamics of multiple objects in a video sequence efficiently. In this paper, we propose a Transformer-based long-term and short-term memory framework for MOT, enhancing online object tracking with improved feature representation and association mechanisms. Specifically, we employ an improved backbone network to extract highly discriminative object features, followed by a Transformer-based feature encoder to generate object embeddings. The Transformer decoder utilizes detection embeddings to locate new objects and tracking embeddings to refine existing trajectories. To model object motion dynamics and maintain long-term memory, we integrate a KAN-enhanced Gated Recurrent Unit (GRU) and a cross-temporal module. Additionally, an adaptive aggregation module is introduced to fuse object features from adjacent frames, mitigating trajectory inconsistencies and enhancing association robustness. Given the presence of multiple objects in video sequences, a memory attention layer is incorporated to generate more discriminative feature representations. Our method effectively addresses object tracking challenges under severe occlusions and rapid motion scenarios by reducing ID switches and improving tracking stability. When evaluated on the widely used MOT benchmark dataset, our approach demonstrates competitive performance, highlighting its potential for online multi-object aerial tracking tasks.

articleTitle: Highway Construction Progress Assessment Based on DeeplabV3+
publicationTitle: 2025 5th International Conference on Consumer Electronics and Computer Engineering (ICCECE)
abstract: In order to conduct comprehensive surveys and quantitative assessments of highway construction projects accurately and rapidly, this paper proposes a new method for highway construction progress assessment that combines remote sensing imagery and deep learning. Firstly, high-resolution remote sensing images of highways that are under construction, are obtained using low-altitude unmanned aerial vehicle technology. A deep learning training dataset is then created. DeepLabV3+deep learning network is employed to train the classification model for construction progress assessment. Comparative experiments based on U-net and the maximum likelihood estimate are carried out. The experiment demonstrates that the classification results based on DeeplabV3+ are superior to those of U-net and maximum likelihood estimate, providing necessary data and technical support for the assessment of highway construction progress. Additionally, we evaluated the robustness of this model in terms of image resolution, image noise, and application scenarios. We also drew some conclusions that are helpful for the application of deep learning in engineering.

articleTitle: Personalized Recommendation Systems Based on Multi-Source Heterogeneous Data
publicationTitle: 2025 5th International Conference on Consumer Electronics and Computer Engineering (ICCECE)
abstract: With the rapid development of Internet technology and the widespread generation of multi-source heterogeneous data, various types of data such as user behavior, social relationships, and text information jointly depict the complex and changeable interests and preferences of users. However, traditional recommendation system faces challenges in effectively integrating heterogeneous information sources and providing diverse recommendation results, often leading to limited recommendation diversity and suboptimal user satisfaction when processing these data. In order to solve the challenge resulting from the diversity of user interests and the fusion of multi-source heterogeneous data. Traditional multimodal fusion techniques predominantly depend on predetermined methodologies for integrating diverse data sources. However, these conventional approaches often prove inadequate in comprehensively capturing the intricate interdependencies among the data sources, consequently leading to suboptimal performance in recommendation systems. Therefore, we proposed a recommendation framework named GraphSelfRec, the fundamental new of GraphSelfRec lies in its development of a multi-level adaptive attention mechanism, which dynamically adjusts the weights of different data sources and effectively captures the heterogeneous nature of user interests through its fusion strategy. In addition, the framework introduces efficient neighbor sampling and graph compression techniques to meet the needs of large-scale data scenarios. Experimental results show that the proposed model significantly outperform existing methods in terms of recommendation accuracy and diversity, while also achieving high efficiency and transparency.

articleTitle: Optimization Method for Communication Security in Millimeter Wave and Fiber Hybrid Networks Based on Machine Learning
publicationTitle: 2025 5th International Conference on Consumer Electronics and Computer Engineering (ICCECE)
abstract: With 5G and 6G's rise, millimeter wave and fiber hybrid networks are gaining popularity for their high data rates and low latency. Yet, they confront significant security issues during transmission. This paper presents a machine learning-based communication security optimization method for these networks. It involves creating a channel model and applying ML algorithms to enhance channel prediction and optimization, thereby boosting transmission security and efficiency. Experiments demonstrate the method's effectiveness in lowering bit error rates, increasing signal-to-noise ratios, and bolstering the system's anti-interference capabilities.

articleTitle: Research on Comfort Control of Smart Home Environment Based on Deep Reinforcement Learning
publicationTitle: 2025 5th International Conference on Consumer Electronics and Computer Engineering (ICCECE)
abstract: The comfort of the indoor environment and the energy consumption of smart devices are key issues in smart home research. The comfort of the indoor environment directly affects the physical and mental health of people working and living in it, while the control of energy consumption helps to realize low-carbon environmental protection and cost savings. Currently, the mainstream programs of “whole-house intelligence” in the market are based on logic control and scenario control. These programs are often simple and effective but cannot effectively balance indoor comfort and power consumption. Domestic and international scholars' research on indoor comfort control focuses more on modeling by understanding the user's habit of using the equipment and the condition of the equipment. However, users do not know how to operate or make mistakes in operation will cause obstacles to model learning, and this control method lacks objective and effective control standards. Therefore, in order to solve the above problems, this paper proposes an autonomous smart device control method based on the deep reinforcement learning method, taking the illumination and temperature environments in the indoor environment as the research objects. The main contributions are as follows: 1) By using the DQN method to solve the device control problem, the energy consumption is significantly reduced while ensuring comfort compared to PID and MPC schemes. 2) The environment is feature extracted to express the indoor comfort level more accurately. At the same time, the state space dimension of the DQN method is reduced, and the performance of the DQN method is improved. 3) The indoor temperature comfort is calculated using the BP neural network, and the feature extraction ability of temperature comfort is improved under the condition of limited parameters.
